passages.vernacularMandarin: 船長當時相當年輕、瘦削活躍,甚至在身材上都帶有威爾士血統痕跡,因為他相當矮。他以日薪兩元的機械工身分,從鄰近約翰斯敦工廠來到我們這裡。我們很快看到他是個人物。每個動作都顯示出來。他在內戰期間志願做列兵,表現出色,成為一個從未退縮的連的連長。埃德加·湯姆森工廠大部分成功屬於這個人。

passages.original: In later years he declined an interest in the firm which would have made him a millionaire. I told him one day that some of the young men who had been given an interest were now making much more than he was and we had voted to make him a partner. This entailed no financial responsibility, as we always provided that the cost of the interest given was payable only out of profits.
passages.vernacular: 後來佢婉拒公司權益,該權益會令佢成為百萬富翁。有一日我告訴佢,一些獲給予權益嘅年輕人現在賺得比佢多得多,我哋已投票令佢成為合夥人。這不涉及財務責任,因為我哋總是規定所給權益嘅成本只從利潤中支付。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來他婉拒公司權益,該權益會使他成為百萬富翁。有一天我告訴他,一些獲給予權益的年輕人現在賺得比他多得多,我們已投票使他成為合夥人。這不涉及財務責任,因為我們總是規定所給權益的成本只從利潤中支付。

passages.original: "No," he said, "I don't want to have my thoughts running on business. I have enough trouble looking after these works. Just give me a h--l of a salary if you think I'm worth it."
passages.vernacular: 「唔,」佢講,「我唔想我嘅思想一直想住生意。我睇住呢啲工廠已經夠麻煩。如果你覺得我值,就畀我一個地獄般嘅薪水。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,」他說,「我不想我的思想一直想著生意。我看著這些工廠已經夠麻煩。如果你覺得我值,就給我一個地獄般的薪水。」

passages.original: "All right, Captain, the salary of the President of the United States is yours."
passages.vernacular: 「好,船長,美國總統嘅薪水歸你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,船長,美國總統的薪水歸你。」

passages.original: "That's the talk," said the little Welshman.
passages.vernacular: 「咁就啱,」細小嘅威爾士人講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就對,」小小的威爾士人說。

passages.original: "Peacock, what would you give to be made a millionaire?"
passages.vernacular: 「皮科克,你願意付出幾多成為百萬富翁?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「皮科克,你願意付出多少成為百萬富翁?」

passages.original: "A liberal discount for cash, sir," was the answer.
passages.vernacular: 「現金慷慨折扣,先生,」係答案。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現金慷慨折扣,先生,」是答案。

passages.original: He was a partner owning a two per cent interest when the Carnegie Steel Company was merged into the United States Steel Corporation.]
passages.vernacular: 卡內基鋼鐵公司併入美國鋼鐵公司時,佢是持有百分之二權益的合夥人。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卡內基鋼鐵公司併入美國鋼鐵公司時,他是持有百分之二權益的合夥人。]

passages.original: Our competitors in steel were at first disposed to ignore us. Knowing the difficulties they had in starting their own steel works, they could not believe we would be ready to deliver rails for another year and declined to recognize us as competitors. The price of steel rails when we began was about seventy dollars per ton. We sent our agent through the country with instructions to take orders at the best prices he could obtain; and before our competitors knew it, we had obtained a large number--quite sufficient to justify us in making a start.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅鋼鐵競爭對手起初傾向忽視我哋。知道佢哋自己開辦鋼廠時嘅困難,佢哋不相信我哋一年內準備好交付鋼軌,拒絕承認我哋是競爭對手。我哋開始時鋼軌價格約每噸七十元。我哋派代理走遍全國,指示佢以所能取得嘅最好價格接單;我哋嘅競爭對手未察覺之前,我哋已取得大量訂單——足以證明我哋開始是合理的。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的鋼鐵競爭對手起初傾向忽視我們。知道他們自己開辦鋼廠時的困難,他們不相信我們一年內準備好交付鋼軌,拒絕承認我們是競爭對手。我們開始時鋼軌價格約每噸七十元。我們派代理走遍全國,指示他以所能取得的最好價格接單;我們的競爭對手未察覺之前,我們已取得大量訂單——足以證明我們開始是合理的。

passages.original: So perfect was the machinery, so admirable the plans, so skillful were the men selected by Captain Jones, and so great a manager was he himself, that our success was phenomenal. I think I place a unique statement on record when I say that the result of the first month's operations left a margin of profit of $11,000. It is also remarkable that so perfect was our system of accounts that we knew the exact amount of the profit. We had learned from experience in our iron works what exact accounting meant. There is nothing more profitable than clerks to check up each transfer of material from one department to another in process of manufacture.
passages.vernacular: 機器如此完美,計劃如此出色,瓊斯船長所選之人如此熟練,佢自己係如此偉大嘅經理,以致我哋嘅成功係驚人嘅。我想我記錄咗獨一無二嘅說法:頭一個月運作嘅結果,留下一萬一千元利潤。同樣值得注意的是,我哋賬目制度如此完美,我哋知道利潤的確切數額。我哋從鐵廠經驗中學到精確記賬的意義。冇乜比文員核對製造過程中物料從一個部門轉移到另一個部門更賺錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 機器如此完美,計劃如此出色,瓊斯船長所選之人如此熟練,他自己是如此偉大的經理,以致我們的成功是驚人的。我想我記錄了獨一無二的說法:頭一個月運作的結果,留下一萬一千元利潤。同樣值得注意的是,我們賬目制度如此完美,我們知道利潤的確切數額。我們從鐵廠經驗中學到精確記賬的意義。沒什麼比文員核對製造過程中物料從一個部門轉移到另一個部門更賺錢。

passages.original: The new venture in steel having started off so promisingly, I began to think of taking a holiday, and my long-cherished purpose of going around the world came to the front. Mr. J.W. Vandevort ("Vandy") and I accordingly set out in the autumn of 1878. I took with me several pads suitable for penciling and began to make a few notes day by day, not with any intention of publishing a book; but thinking, perhaps, I might print a few copies of my notes for private circulation. The sensation which one has when he first sees his remarks in the form of a printed book is great. When the package came from the printers I re-read the book trying to decide whether it was worth while to send copies to my friends. I came to the conclusion that upon the whole it was best to do so and await the verdict.
passages.vernacular: 鋼鐵新事業起步如此有前景,我開始想放假,我長久懷抱嘅環遊世界目標浮現。J·W·范德沃特先生(「范迪」)同我因此於1878年秋出發。我帶咗幾本適合用鉛筆寫嘅簿,開始每日記少少筆記,並非打算出書;而是想也許可以印幾份筆記私人傳閱。第一次見到自己嘅話以印刷書本形式出現,感覺好強烈。印刷商嘅包裹寄到時,我重讀書,試圖決定值不值得送畀朋友。我得出結論:整體而言最好送,然後等待判決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鋼鐵新事業起步如此有前景,我開始想放假,我長久懷抱的環遊世界目標浮現。J·W·范德沃特先生(「范迪」)和我因此於1878年秋出發。我帶了幾本適合用鉛筆寫的簿,開始每天記一點筆記,並非打算出書;而是想也許可以印幾份筆記私人傳閱。第一次看到自己的話以印刷書本形式出現,感覺很強烈。印刷商的包裹寄到時,我重讀書,試圖決定值不值得送給朋友。我得出結論:整體而言最好送,然後等待判決。

passages.original: The writer of a book designed for his friends has no reason to anticipate an unkind reception, but there is always some danger of its being damned with faint praise. The responses in my case, however, exceeded expectations, and were of such a character as to satisfy me that the writers really had enjoyed the book, or meant at least a part of what they said about it. Every author is prone to believe sweet words. Among the first that came were in a letter from Anthony Drexel, Philadelphia's great banker, complaining that I had robbed him of several hours of sleep. Having begun the book he could not lay it down and retired at two o'clock in the morning after finishing. Several similar letters were received. I remember Mr. Huntington, president of the Central Pacific Railway, meeting me one morning and saying he was going to pay me a great compliment.
passages.vernacular: 為朋友而寫書嘅作者冇理由預期不友善嘅接待,不過總有被淡淡稱讚所毀的危險。不過就我而言,回應超出預期,而且性質令我滿意:寫信人真嘅享受呢本書,或至少係真心認同佢哋對佢所講嘅一部分。每個作者都傾向相信甜言蜜語。最早到的當中有費城大銀行家安東尼·德雷克塞爾的信,投訴我奪走佢幾個鐘頭睡眠。開始讀這本書後,他放不下,讀完後凌晨兩點才就寢。收到幾封類似嘅信。我記得中央太平洋鐵路總裁亨廷頓先生一個朝早遇到我,話佢要對我作極大的恭維。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為朋友而寫書的作者沒理由預期不友善的接待,不過總有被淡淡稱讚所毀的危險。不過就我而言,回應超出預期,而且性質使我滿意:寫信人真的享受這本書,或至少是真心認同他們對它所說的一部分。每個作者都傾向相信甜言蜜語。最早到的當中有費城大銀行家安東尼·德雷克塞爾的信,投訴我奪走他幾個鐘頭睡眠。開始讀這本書後,他放不下,讀完後凌晨兩點才就寢。收到幾封類似的信。我記得中央太平洋鐵路總裁亨廷頓先生一個早上遇到我,說他要對我作極大的恭維。

passages.original: "What is it?" Tasked.
passages.vernacular: 「咩話?」我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼?」我問。

passages.original: "Oh, I read your book from end to end."
passages.vernacular: 「噢,我由頭到尾讀咗你本書。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「噢,我從頭到尾讀了你那本書。」

passages.original: "Well," I said, "that is not such a great compliment. Others of our mutual friends have done that."
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,」我講,「呢不算好大嘅恭維。我哋其他共同朋友都做過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,」我說,「這不算很大的恭維。我們其他共同朋友都做過。」

passages.original: "Oh, yes, but probably none of your friends are like me. I have not read a book for years except my ledger and I did not intend to read yours, but when I began it I could not lay it down. My ledger is the only book I have gone through for five years."
passages.vernacular: 「噢,係,不過你嘅朋友大概冇一個似我。我多年冇讀過書,除咗我嘅分類賬,我原本冇打算讀你嘅,不過一開始就放唔低。我嘅分類賬係我五年來唯一讀完嘅書。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「噢,是,不過你的朋友大概沒一個像我。我多年沒讀過書,除了我的分類賬,我原本沒打算讀你的,不過一開始就放不下。我的分類賬是我五年來唯一讀完的書。」

passages.original: I was not disposed to credit all that my friends said, but others who had obtained the book from them were pleased with it and I lived for some months under intoxicating, but I trust not perilously pernicious, flattery. Several editions of the book were printed to meet the request for copies. Some notices of it and extracts got into the papers, and finally Charles Scribner's Sons asked to publish it for the market. So "Round the World" came before the public and I was at last "an author."
passages.vernacular: 我唔願相信朋友哋所講嘅一切,不過從佢哋嗰度得到書嘅其他人都喜歡,我生活喺令人陶醉(但我相信並非危險有害)嘅奉承下好幾個月。為滿足索取副本嘅要求,書印咗幾個版本。一些評論同摘錄見報,終於查爾斯·斯克里布納父子公司要求出版上市。於是《環遊世界》面世,我終於成為「作家」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不願相信朋友們所說的一切,不過從他們那裡得到書的其他人都喜歡,我生活在令人陶醉(但我相信並非危險有害)的奉承下好幾個月。為滿足索取副本的要求,書印了幾個版本。一些評論和摘錄見報,終於查爾斯·斯克里布納父子公司要求出版上市。於是《環遊世界》面世,我終於成為「作家」。

passages.original: A new horizon was opened up to me by this voyage. It quite changed my intellectual outlook. Spencer and Darwin were then high in the zenith, and I had become deeply interested in their work. I began to view the various phases of human life from the standpoint of the evolutionist. In China I read Confucius; in India, Buddha and the sacred books of the Hindoos; among the Parsees, in Bombay, I studied Zoroaster. The result of my journey was to bring a certain mental peace. Where there had been chaos there was now order. My mind was at rest. I had a philosophy at last. The words of Christ "The Kingdom of Heaven is within you," had a new meaning for me. Not in the past or in the future, but now and here is Heaven within us. All our duties lie in this world and in the present, and trying impatiently to peer into that which lies beyond is as vain as fruitless.
passages.vernacular: 呢次航行為我開闢新視野。佢完全改變咗我嘅知識眼界。斯賓塞同達爾文當時如日中天,我對佢哋嘅著作深感興趣。我開始從進化論者角度睇人類生活嘅各個階段。喺中國我讀孔子;喺印度,佛陀同印度教聖典;喺孟買嘅帕西人當中,我研究瑣羅亞斯德。我旅程嘅結果係帶嚟某種心靈平靜。曾經混亂之處,而家有秩序。我嘅心安息。我終於有咗哲學。基督嘅話「天國就喺你哋心裡」對我有咗新意義。天堂不喺過去或將來,而喺我哋心中此時此地。我哋所有職責都喺呢個世界、當下,不耐煩地試圖窺探彼岸之物係徒然無果嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次航行為我開闢新視野。它完全改變了我的知識眼界。斯賓塞和達爾文當時如日中天,我對他們的著作深感興趣。我開始從進化論者角度看人類生活的各個階段。在中國我讀孔子;在印度,佛陀和印度教聖典;在孟買的帕西人當中,我研究瑣羅亞斯德。我旅程的結果是帶來某種心靈平靜。曾經混亂之處,現在有秩序。我的心安息。我終於有了哲學。基督的話「天國就在你們心裡」對我有了新意義。天堂不在過去或將來,而在我們心中此時此地。我們所有職責都在這個世界、當下,不耐煩地試圖窺探彼岸之物是徒然無果的。

passages.original: All the remnants of theology in which I had been born and bred, all the impressions that Swedenborg had made upon me, now ceased to influence me or to occupy my thoughts. I found that no nation had all the truth in the revelation it regards as divine, and no tribe is so low as to be left without some truth; that every people has had its great teacher; Buddha for one; Confucius for another; Zoroaster for a third; Christ for a fourth. The teachings of all these I found ethically akin so that I could say with Matthew Arnold, one I was so proud to call friend:
passages.vernacular: 我所出生長大嘅神學所有殘餘,斯威登堡畀我嘅所有印象,而家唔再影響我或佔據我嘅思想。我發現沒有一個國家擁有佢視為神聖啟示中的全部真理,亦沒有一個部落低到沒有一些真理;每個民族都有其偉大導師;一個是佛陀,另一個是孔子,第三個是瑣羅亞斯德,第四個是基督。我發現所有呢啲教導喺倫理上相近,以致我可以同馬修·阿諾德一起講,佢係我好驕傲稱為朋友嘅:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我所出生長大的神學所有殘餘,斯威登堡給我的所有印象,現在不再影響我或佔據我的思想。我發現沒有一個國家擁有它視為神聖啟示中的全部真理,也沒有一個部落低到沒有一些真理;每個民族都有其偉大導師;一個是佛陀,另一個是孔子,第三個是瑣羅亞斯德,第四個是基督。我發現所有這些教導在倫理上相近,以致我可以與馬修·阿諾德一起說,他是我很驕傲稱為朋友的:

passages.original: "Children of men! the unseen Power, whose eye For ever doth accompany mankind Hath looked on no religion scornfully That men did ever find.
passages.vernacular: 「人類嘅子孫啊!嗰睇唔見嘅力量,祂嘅眼睛永遠陪伴人類,從未輕蔑地睇過人類曾找到嘅任何宗教。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「人類的子孫啊!那看不見的力量,祂的眼睛永遠陪伴人類,從未輕蔑地看過人類曾找到的任何宗教。

passages.original: Which has not taught weak wills how much they can? Which has not fall'n in the dry heart like rain? Which has not cried to sunk, self-weary man, Thou must be born again."
passages.vernacular: 邊一個冇教導軟弱嘅意志,佢哋能做到多少?邊一個冇如雨落喺乾涸嘅心中?邊一個冇向沉淪、厭倦自己嘅人呼喊:你必須重生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哪一個沒有教導軟弱的意志,他們能做到多少?哪一個沒有如雨落在乾涸的心中?哪一個沒有向沉淪、厭倦自己的人呼喊:你必須重生。」

passages.original: "The Light of Asia," by Edwin Arnold, came out at this time and gave me greater delight than any similar poetical work I had recently read. I had just been in India and the book took me there again. My appreciation of it reached the author's ears and later having made his acquaintance in London, he presented me with the original manuscript of the book. It is one of my most precious treasures. Every person who can, even at a sacrifice, make the voyage around the world should do so. All other travel compared to it seems incomplete, gives us merely vague impressions of parts of the whole. When the circle has been completed, you feel on your return that you have seen (of course only in the mass) all there is to be seen. The parts fit into one symmetrical whole and you see humanity wherever it is placed working out a destiny tending to one definite end.
passages.vernacular: 愛德溫·阿諾德嘅《亞洲之光》喺此時出版,比我最近讀過嘅任何類似詩作都令我更喜悅。我剛從印度回嚟,呢本書又將我帶回嗰度。我對它嘅欣賞傳到作者耳中,後來我在倫敦認識他,他送了我該書原稿。佢係我最珍貴嘅寶物之一。每個人,只要能夠,即使犧牲,都應該環遊世界。同之相比,所有其他旅行似乎不完整,只畀我哋對整體部分嘅模糊印象。當圓圈完成時,你返回時覺得(當然只係整體上)你已見到所有可見嘅。各部分組成一個對稱的整體,你看到無論人類身處何方,都在實現傾向於一個明確終點的命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 愛德溫·阿諾德的《亞洲之光》在此時出版,比我最近讀過的任何類似詩作都使我更喜悅。我剛從印度回來,這本書又將我帶回那裡。我對它的欣賞傳到作者耳中,後來我在倫敦認識他,他送了我該書原稿。它是我最珍貴的寶物之一。每個人,只要能夠,即使犧牲,都應該環遊世界。與之相比,所有其他旅行似乎不完整,只給我們對整體部分的模糊印象。當圓圈完成時,你回來時覺得(當然只是整體上)你已看到所有可見的。各部分組成一個對稱的整體,你看到無論人類身處何方,都在實現傾向於一個明確終點的命運。

passages.original: The world traveler who gives careful study to the bibles of the various religions of the East will be well repaid. The conclusion reached will be that the inhabitants of each country consider their own religion the best of all. They rejoice that their lot has been cast where it is, and are disposed to pity the less fortunate condemned to live beyond their sacred limits. The masses of all nations are usually happy, each mass certain that:
passages.vernacular: 仔細研究東方各種宗教經典嘅世界旅行者將得到豐厚回報。得出嘅結論將係,每個國家嘅居民都認為自己嘅宗教最好。佢哋為自己嘅命運落喺邊度而高興,並傾向於憐憫嗰啲被注定生活喺神聖界限之外嘅較不幸者。所有國家嘅大眾通常都快樂,各自肯定:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仔細研究東方各種宗教經典的世界旅行者將得到豐厚回報。得出的結論將是,每個國家的居民都認為自己的宗教最好。他們為自己的命運落在哪裡而高興,並傾向於憐憫那些被注定生活在神聖界限之外的較不幸者。所有國家的大眾通常都快樂,各自肯定:

passages.original: "East or West Home is best."
passages.vernacular: 「東或西,家最好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「東或西,家最好。」

passages.original: Two illustrations of this from our "Round the World" trip may be noted:
passages.vernacular: 我哋「環遊世界」旅程可以注意兩個例子:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們「環遊世界」旅程可以注意兩個例子:

passages.original: Visiting the tapioca workers in the woods near Singapore, we found them busily engaged, the children running about stark naked, the parents clothed in the usual loose rags. Our party attracted great attention. We asked our guide to tell the people that we came from a country where the water in such a pond as that before us would become solid at this season of the year and we could walk upon it and that sometimes it would be so hard horses and wagons crossed wide rivers on the ice. They wondered and asked why we didn't come and live among them. They really were very happy.
passages.vernacular: 參觀新加坡附近樹林中嘅木薯工人時,我哋發現佢哋忙碌工作,孩子們赤身裸體跑來跑去,父母穿著慣常寬鬆破布。我哋一行引起極大關注。我哋請嚮導告訴人們,我哋來自一個國家,在這個季節,像面前那樣一個池塘的水會變成固體,我們可以在上面行走,有時硬得馬和馬車可以在冰上過寬闊的河。佢哋驚奇,問我哋點解不嚟同佢哋一起住。佢哋確實非常快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 參觀新加坡附近樹林中的木薯工人時,我們發現他們忙碌工作,孩子們赤身裸體跑來跑去,父母穿著慣常寬鬆破布。我們一行引起極大關注。我們請嚮導告訴人們,我們來自一個國家,在這個季節,像面前那樣一個池塘的水會變成固體,我們可以在上面行走,有時硬得馬和馬車可以在冰上過寬闊的河。他們驚奇,問我們為什麼不來和他們一起住。他們確實非常快樂。

passages.original: Again:
passages.vernacular: 再者:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再者:

passages.original: On the way to the North Cape we visited a reindeer camp of the Laplanders. A sailor from the ship was deputed to go with the party. I walked homeward with him, and as we approached the fiord looking down and over to the opposite shore we saw a few straggling huts and one two-story house under construction. What is that new building for? we asked.
passages.vernacular: 去北角途中,我哋參觀拉普蘭人嘅馴鹿營地。船上一名水手被派隨團。我同佢步行回家,接近峽灣時,我哋往下望向對岸,睇到幾間零散嘅小屋同一座建造中嘅兩層房屋。新建築是做咩用的?我們問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去北角途中,我們參觀拉普蘭人的馴鹿營地。船上一名水手被派隨團。我與他步行回家,接近峽灣時,我們往下望向對岸,看到幾間零散的小屋和一座建造中的兩層房屋。新建築是做什麼用的?我們問。

passages.original: "That is to be the home of a man born in Tromso who has made a great deal of money and has now come back to spend his days there. He is very rich."
passages.vernacular: 「嗰將係一位喺特羅姆瑟出生、賺咗好多錢、而家回嚟喺嗰度度過晚年嘅人嘅家。佢好富有。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那將是一位在特羅姆瑟出生、賺了很多錢、現在回來在那裡度過晚年的人的家。他很富有。」

passages.original: "You told me you had travelled all over the world. You have seen London, New York, Calcutta, Melbourne, and other places. If you made a fortune like that man what place would you make your home in old age?" His eye glistened as he said:
passages.vernacular: 「你告訴我你走遍世界。你見過倫敦、紐約、加爾各答、墨爾本,同其他地方。如果你賺到像嗰人嗰樣嘅財富,你晚年會喺邊度安家?」佢眼睛發亮講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你告訴我你走遍世界。你見過倫敦、紐約、加爾各答、墨爾本,和其他地方。如果你賺到像那人那樣的財富,你晚年會在哪裡安家?」他眼睛發亮說:

passages.original: "Ah, there's no place like Tromso." This is in the arctic circle, six months of night, but he had been born in Tromso. Home, sweet, sweet home!
passages.vernacular: 「啊,冇地方像特羅姆瑟。」呢喺北極圈內,六個月黑夜,但佢喺特羅姆瑟出生。家,甜蜜,甜蜜嘅家!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「啊,沒有地方像特羅姆瑟。」這在北極圈內,六個月黑夜,但他在特羅姆瑟出生。家,甜蜜,甜蜜的家!

passages.original: Among the conditions of life or the laws of nature, some of which seem to us faulty, some apparently unjust and merciless, there are many that amaze us by their beauty and sweetness. Love of home, regardless of its character or location, certainly is one of these. And what a pleasure it is to find that, instead of the Supreme Being confining revelation to one race or nation, every race has the message best adapted for it in its present stage of development. The Unknown Power has neglected none.
passages.vernacular: 生活嘅條件或自然嘅法則中,有些喺我哋看來有缺陷,有些顯然不公正無情,但都有許多以其美麗同甜蜜令我哋驚嘆。對家嘅愛,不論其性質或位置,肯定係其中之一。發現至高者並未將啟示局限於一個種族或國家,而係每個種族都有最適合其現階段發展嘅訊息,係何等樂事。未知嘅力量冇忽略任何一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 生活的條件或自然的法則中,有些在我們看來有缺陷,有些顯然不公正無情,但也有許多以其美麗和甜蜜令我們驚嘆。對家的愛,不論其性質或位置,肯定是其中之一。發現至高者並未將啟示局限於一個種族或國家,而是每個種族都有最適合其現階段發展的訊息,是何等樂事。未知的力量沒有忽略任何一個。

chapters.title: Coaching Trip and Marriage 馬車旅行與婚姻

passages.original: The Freedom of my native town (Dunfermline) was conferred upon me July 12, 1877, the first Freedom and the greatest honor I ever received. I was overwhelmed. Only two signatures upon the roll came between mine and Sir Walter Scott's, who had been made a Burgess. My parents had seen him one day sketching Dunfermline Abbey and often told me about his appearance. My speech in reply to the Freedom was the subject of much concern. I spoke to my Uncle Bailie Morrison, telling him I just felt like saying so and so, as this really was in my heart. He was an orator himself and he spoke words of wisdom to me then.
passages.vernacular: 1877年7月12日,我家鄉鄧弗姆林授予我自由市民權,係我收過第一個自由市民權,亦係最大嘅榮譽。我受寵若驚。名冊上我同沃爾特·司各特爵士(佢曾被授予市民權)之間只相隔兩個簽名。我父母有一日見過佢寫生鄧弗姆林修道院,經常同我講佢嘅外貌。我答謝自由市民權嘅演講,令我好擔心。我同我嘅貝利莫里森叔叔講,話我只覺得想講某某,因為呢個真係在我心裡。佢自己係演說家,當時講咗智慧之言畀我聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1877年7月12日,我家鄉鄧弗姆林授予我自由市民權,是我收過第一個自由市民權,也是最大的榮譽。我受寵若驚。名冊上我與沃爾特·司各特爵士(他曾被授予市民權)之間只相隔兩個簽名。我父母有一天見過他寫生鄧弗姆林修道院,經常跟我講他的外貌。我答謝自由市民權的演講,使我很擔心。我跟我的貝利莫里森叔叔說,說我只覺得想說某某,因為這個真是在我心裡。他自己是演說家,當時說了智慧之言給我聽。

passages.original: "Just say that, Andra; nothing like saying just what you really feel."
passages.vernacular: 「就咁講,安德拉;冇乜比講出你真正感受更好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就這樣說,安德拉;沒什麼比說出你真正感受更好。」

passages.original: It was a lesson in public speaking which I took to heart. There is one rule I might suggest for youthful orators. When you stand up before an audience reflect that there are before you only men and women. You should speak to them as you speak to other men and women in daily intercourse. If you are not trying to be something different from yourself, there is no more occasion for embarrassment than if you were talking in your office to a party of your own people--none whatever. It is trying to be other than one's self that unmans one. Be your own natural self and go ahead. I once asked Colonel Ingersoll, the most effective public speaker I ever heard, to what he attributed his power. "Avoid elocutionists like snakes," he said, "and be yourself."
passages.vernacular: 呢是我銘記於心嘅一堂演講課。我可以向年輕演說家建議一條規則。當你站喺聽眾面前,想想你面前只有男人同女人。你應該同佢哋講話,就好似你日常交往中同其他男女講話一樣。如果你不嘗試成為與自己不同嘅人,冇更多理由尷尬,就好似你在辦公室同一班自己人傾偈一樣——完全冇。正是嘗試成為自己以外嘅人,令人失去勇氣。做你自然嘅自己,然後繼續。我曾問英格索爾上校(我聽過最有效嘅公眾演說家)佢嘅力量歸功於咩。「像避蛇一樣避開演說術教師,」佢講,「然後做你自己。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我銘記於心的一堂演講課。我可以向年輕演說家建議一條規則。當你站在聽眾面前,想想你面前只有男人和女人。你應該跟他們說話,就像你日常交往中跟其他男女說話一樣。如果你不嘗試成為與自己不同的人,沒更多理由尷尬,就像你在辦公室跟一班自己人交談一樣——完全沒。正是嘗試成為自己以外的人,使人失去勇氣。做你自然的自己,然後繼續。我曾問英格索爾上校(我聽過最有效的公眾演說家)他的力量歸功於什麼。「像避蛇一樣避開演說術教師,」他說,「然後做你自己。」

passages.original: I spoke again at Dunfermline, July 27, 1881, when my mother laid the foundation stone there of the first free library building I ever gave. My father was one of five weavers who founded the earliest library in the town by opening their own books to their neighbors. Dunfermline named the building I gave "Carnegie Library." The architect asked for my coat of arms. I informed him I had none, but suggested that above the door there might be carved a rising sun shedding its rays with the motto: "Let there be light." This he adopted.
passages.vernacular: 我於1881年7月27日再次在鄧弗姆林發言,當時我媽媽在嗰度為我捐贈嘅第一座免費圖書館大樓奠基。我爸爸係五個織工之一,佢哋向鄰居開放自己嘅書,創辦咗鎮上最早嘅圖書館。鄧弗姆林將我捐贈嘅大樓命名為「卡內基圖書館」。建築師問我要紋章。我告訴佢我冇,不過建議門上可以雕刻一個升起的太陽,灑下光芒,附座右銘:「讓光明降臨。」佢採納了。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我於1881年7月27日再次在鄧弗姆林發言,當時我母親在那裡為我捐贈的第一座免費圖書館大樓奠基。我父親是五個織工之一,他們向鄰居開放自己的書,創辦了鎮上最早的圖書館。鄧弗姆林將我捐贈的大樓命名為「卡內基圖書館」。建築師問我要紋章。我告訴他我沒有,不過建議門上可以雕刻一個升起的太陽,灑下光芒,附座右銘:「讓光明降臨。」他採納了。

passages.original: We had come up to Dunfermline with a coaching party. When walking through England in the year 1867 with George Lauder and Harry Phipps I had formed the idea of coaching from Brighton to Inverness with a party of my dearest friends. The time had come for the long-promised trip, and in the spring of 1881 we sailed from New York, a party of eleven, to enjoy one of the happiest excursions of my life. It was one of the holidays from business that kept me young and happy--worth all the medicine in the world.
passages.vernacular: 我哋乘馬車旅行團來到鄧弗姆林。1867年我同喬治·勞德同哈利·菲普斯步行穿越英格蘭時,我產生咗與一班我最親愛嘅朋友乘馬車從布萊頓去因弗內斯嘅念頭。期待已久嘅旅行時間到了,1881年春,我哋一行十一人從紐約啟航,享受我一生最快樂嘅遠足之一。呢是使我保持年輕快樂嘅商業假期之一——抵過世上所有藥物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們乘馬車旅行團來到鄧弗姆林。1867年我與喬治·勞德和哈利·菲普斯步行穿越英格蘭時,我產生了與一班我最親愛的朋友乘馬車從布萊頓去因弗內斯的念頭。期待已久的旅行時間到了,1881年春,我們一行十一人從紐約啟航,享受我一生最快樂的遠足之一。這是使我保持年輕快樂的商業假期之一——抵過世上所有藥物。

passages.original: All the notes I made of the coaching trip were a few lines a day in twopenny pass-books bought before we started. As with "Round the World," I thought that I might some day write a magazine article, or give some account of my excursion for those who accompanied me; but one wintry day I decided that it was scarcely worth while to go down to the New York office, three miles distant, and the question was how I should occupy the spare time. I thought of the coaching trip, and decided to write a few lines just to see how I should get on. The narrative flowed freely, and before the day was over I had written between three and four thousand words. I took up the pleasing task every stormy day when it was unnecessary for me to visit the office, and in exactly twenty sittings I had finished a book. I handed the notes to Scribner's people and asked them to print a few hundred copies for private circulation. The volume pleased my friends, as "Round the World" had done. Mr. Champlin one day told me that Mr. Scribner had read the book and would like very much to publish it for general circulation upon his own account, subject to a royalty.
passages.vernacular: 我為馬車旅行作的所有筆記,只係出發前買嘅兩便士記賬簿上每日幾行。同《環遊世界》一樣,我以為有一日可能寫一篇雜誌文章,或為同行者作些遠足記述;不過一個寒冷嘅日子,我決定不值得去三英里外嘅紐約辦公室,問題是怎樣利用空閒時間。我想起馬車旅行,決定寫幾行睇下進展如何。敘述流暢,一日未完我已寫咗三四千字。每個風雨日我無須去辦公室時,我都做呢件愉快嘅工作,恰好二十次坐下,我就完成咗一本書。我將筆記交畀斯克里布納公司嘅人,請佢哋印幾百份私人傳閱。呢本書令我朋友高興,一如《環遊世界》。錢普林先生有一日告訴我,斯克里布納先生讀過呢本書,好想自己出版供公眾傳閱,按版稅支付。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為馬車旅行作的所有筆記,只是出發前買的兩便士記賬簿上每天幾行。和《環遊世界》一樣,我以為有一天可能寫一篇雜誌文章,或為同行者作些遠足記述;不過一個寒冷的日子,我決定不值得去三英里外的紐約辦公室,問題是怎樣利用空閒時間。我想起馬車旅行,決定寫幾行看看進展如何。敘述流暢,一天未完我已寫了三四千字。每個風雨日我無須去辦公室時,我都做這件愉快的工作,恰好二十次坐下,我就完成了一本書。我將筆記交給斯克里布納公司的人,請他們印幾百份私人傳閱。這本書使我朋友高興,一如《環遊世界》。錢普林先生有一天告訴我,斯克里布納先生讀過這本書,很想自己出版供公眾傳閱,按版稅支付。

passages.original: The vain author is easily persuaded that what he has done is meritorious, and I consented. [Every year this still nets me a small sum in royalties. And thirty years have gone by, 1912.] The letters I received upon the publication of it were so numerous and some so gushing that my people saved them and they are now bound together in scrapbook form, to which additions are made from time to time. The number of invalids who have been pleased to write me, stating that the book had brightened their lives, has been gratifying. Its reception in Britain was cordial; the "Spectator" gave it a favorable review. But any merit that the book has comes, I am sure, from the total absence of effort on my part to make an impression. I wrote for my friends; and what one does easily, one does well. I reveled in the writing of the book, as I had in the journey itself.
passages.vernacular: 虛榮嘅作者容易被說服,相信自己所做的有價值,我同意了。[每年呢仍然為我帶嚟少量版稅。三十年已經過去,1912年。]出版後我收到嘅信件如此多,有些如此洋溢,我家人保存下來,現在裝訂成剪貼簿,不時增添。許多病人樂意寫信畀我,話呢本書令佢哋生活開朗,令我感到欣慰。佢喺英國受到熱情接待;《旁觀者》給予好評。不過我肯定,這本書任何優點,都來自我完全冇努力給人留下印象。我為朋友而寫;輕鬆做嘅事,往往做得好。我陶醉於寫書,如同陶醉於旅程本身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 虛榮的作者容易被說服,相信自己所做的有價值,我同意了。[每年這仍然為我帶來少量版稅。三十年已經過去,1912年。]出版後我收到的信件如此多,有些如此洋溢,我家人保存下來,現在裝訂成剪貼簿,不時增添。許多病人樂意寫信給我,說這本書使他們生活開朗,令我感到欣慰。它在英國受到熱情接待;《旁觀者》給予好評。不過我肯定,這本書任何優點,都來自我完全沒努力給人留下印象。我為朋友而寫;輕鬆做的事,往往做得好。我陶醉於寫書,如同陶醉於旅程本身。

passages.original: The year 1886 ended in deep gloom for me. My life as a happy careless young man, with every want looked after, was over. I was left alone in the world. My mother and brother passed away in November, within a few days of each other, while I lay in bed under a severe attack of typhoid fever, unable to move and, perhaps fortunately, unable to feel the full weight of the catastrophe, being myself face to face with death.
passages.vernacular: 1886年喺深深陰霾中結束。我作為快樂無憂的年輕人,一切需要都有人照顧嘅生活結束了。我被留低在世上孤身一人。我媽媽同細佬在十一月相隔幾日去世,當時我躺喺床上受嚴重傷寒襲擊,動彈不得,也許幸運地,無法感受災難的全部重量,因為我自己正面對死亡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1886年在深深陰霾中結束。我作為快樂無憂的年輕人,一切需要都有人照顧的生活結束了。我被留在世上孤身一人。我母親和弟弟在十一月相隔幾天去世,當時我躺在床上受嚴重傷寒襲擊,動彈不得,也許幸運地,無法感受災難的全部重量,因為我自己正面對死亡。

passages.original: I was the first stricken, upon returning from a visit in the East to our cottage at Cresson Springs on top of the Alleghanies where my mother and I spent our happy summers. I had been quite unwell for a day or two before leaving New York. A physician being summoned, my trouble was pronounced typhoid fever. Professor Dennis was called from New York and he corroborated the diagnosis. An attendant physician and trained nurse were provided at once. Soon after my mother broke down and my brother in Pittsburgh also was reported ill.
passages.vernacular: 我最先病倒,是從東部探訪返嚟,回到我哋在阿勒格尼山頂克雷森泉嘅小屋,我媽媽同我在那裡度過快樂的夏天。我離開紐約前一兩日已相當不適。請咗醫生,我嘅病被診斷為傷寒。丹尼斯教授從紐約被召嚟,證實診斷。即刻安排咗駐診醫生同受訓護士。不久後我媽媽病倒,匹茲堡嘅細佬亦報告生病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最先病倒,是從東部探訪回來,回到我們在阿勒格尼山頂克雷森泉的小屋,我母親和我在那裡度過快樂的夏天。我離開紐約前一兩天已相當不適。請了醫生,我的病被診斷為傷寒。丹尼斯教授從紐約被召來,證實診斷。立刻安排了駐診醫生和受訓護士。不久後我母親病倒,匹茲堡的弟弟也報告生病。

passages.original: I was despaired of, I was so low, and then my whole nature seemed to change. I became reconciled, indulged in pleasing meditations, was without the slightest pain. My mother's and brother's serious condition had not been revealed to me, and when I was informed that both had left me forever it seemed only natural that I should follow them. We had never been separated; why should we be now? But it was decreed otherwise.
passages.vernacular: 我被認為無望,我病得好低,然後我整個本性似乎改變。我變得認命,沉溺於愉快嘅冥想,冇絲毫痛苦。我媽媽同細佬嘅嚴重情況並未向我透露,當我被告知兩人已永遠離開我,似乎自然我應該跟隨佢哋。我哋從未分離;點解而家要?不過天意另有安排。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被認為無望,我病得很低,然後我整個本性似乎改變。我變得認命,沉溺於愉快的冥想,沒絲毫痛苦。我母親和弟弟的嚴重情況並未向我透露,當我被告知兩人已永遠離開我,似乎自然我應該跟隨他們。我們從未分離;為什麼現在要?不過天意另有安排。

passages.original: I recovered slowly and the future began to occupy my thoughts. There was only one ray of hope and comfort in it. Toward that my thoughts always turned. For several years I had known Miss Louise Whitfield. Her mother permitted her to ride with me in the Central Park. We were both very fond of riding. Other young ladies were on my list. I had fine horses and often rode in the Park and around New York with one or the other of the circle. In the end the others all faded into ordinary beings. Miss Whitfield remained alone as the perfect one beyond any I had met. Finally I began to find and admit to myself that she stood the supreme test I had applied to several fair ones in my time. She alone did so of all I had ever known. I could recommend young men to apply this test before offering themselves. If they can honestly believe the following lines, as I did, then all is well:
passages.vernacular: 我慢慢康復,未來開始佔據我思想。其中只有一線希望同安慰。我嘅思想總是轉向嗰度。我認識路易絲·惠特菲爾德小姐已有幾年。佢媽媽准許佢同我在中央公園騎馬。我哋都好鍾意騎馬。我名單上有其他年輕女士。我有好馬,經常喺公園同紐約四周同圈子裡其中一位騎馬。最終其他人都褪色成普通人。惠特菲爾德小姐獨自留下,成為我遇過超越任何人嘅完美者。最終我開始發現並向自己承認,她經得起我曾對幾位佳人應用過嘅最高考驗。我認識嘅所有人當中,只有她做到。我可以建議年輕人喺求婚前應用此考驗。如果佢哋能像我一樣真誠相信以下幾行,一切就好:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我慢慢康復,未來開始佔據我思想。其中只有一線希望和安慰。我的思想總是轉向那裡。我認識路易絲·惠特菲爾德小姐已有幾年。她母親准許她與我在中央公園騎馬。我們都很喜歡騎馬。我名單上有其他年輕女士。我有好馬,經常在公園和紐約四周與圈子裡其中一位騎馬。最終其他人都褪色成普通人。惠特菲爾德小姐獨自留下,成為我遇過超越任何人的完美者。最終我開始發現並向自己承認,她經得起我曾對幾位佳人應用過的最高考驗。我認識的所有人當中,只有她做到。我可以建議年輕人在求婚前應用此考驗。如果他們能像我一樣真誠相信以下幾行,一切就好:

passages.original: "Full many a lady I've eyed with best regard: for several virtues Have I liked several women, never any With so full soul, but some defect in her Did quarrel with the noblest grace she owed, And put it to the foil; but you, O you, So perfect and so peerless are created Of every creature's best."
passages.vernacular: 「許多女子我曾以最佳敬意注視:為了幾種美德我喜歡過幾位女子,從未有任何一位心靈如此完滿,總有些缺陷同佢所擁有嘅最高貴優雅相抵觸,並使之黯然;但你,啊你,被創造得如此完美無雙,集一切造物之最佳。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「許多女子我曾以最佳敬意注視:為了幾種美德我喜歡過幾位女子,從未有任何一位心靈如此完滿,總有些缺陷與她所擁有的最高貴優雅相抵觸,並使之黯然;但你,啊你,被創造得如此完美無雙,集一切造物之最佳。」

passages.original: In my soul I could echo those very words. To-day, after twenty years of life with her, if I could find stronger words I could truthfully use them.
passages.vernacular: 喺我靈魂中,我可以呼應呢啲話。今日,同佢共度二十年後,如果我能找到更有力嘅字,我可以真誠地使用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我靈魂中,我可以呼應這些話。今日,與她共度二十年後,如果我能找到更有力的字,我可以真誠地使用。

passages.original: My advances met with indifferent success. She was not without other and younger admirers. My wealth and future plans were against me. I was rich and had everything and she felt she could be of little use or benefit to me. Her ideal was to be the real helpmeet of a young, struggling man to whom she could and would be indispensable, as her mother had been to her father. The care of her own family had largely fallen upon her after her father's death when she was twenty-one. She was now twenty-eight; her views of life were formed. At times she seemed more favorable and we corresponded. Once, however, she returned my letters saying she felt she must put aside all thought of accepting me.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅追求只得到冷淡嘅成功。佢並非冇其他更年輕嘅追求者。我嘅財富同未來計劃對我不利。我富有,擁有一切,佢覺得自己對我幾乎冇用處或益處。佢嘅理想係做一位年輕、奮鬥男人嘅真正伴侶,對佢佢能夠而且會係不可或缺嘅,正如佢母親對佢父親。佢父親去世後,佢二十一歲時,照顧自己家庭嘅重擔大部分落喺佢身上。佢而家二十八歲;佢對人生嘅看法已形成。有時佢似乎較為贊成,我哋通信。不過有一次,佢退還我嘅信,講佢覺得必須放下接受我嘅所有念頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的追求只得到冷淡的成功。她並非沒有其他更年輕的追求者。我的財富和未來計劃對我不利。我富有,擁有一切,她覺得自己對我幾乎沒有用處或益處。她的理想是做一位年輕、奮鬥男人的真正伴侶,對他她能夠而且會是不可或缺的,正如她母親對她父親。她父親去世後,她二十一歲時,照顧自己家庭的重擔大部分落在她身上。她現在二十八歲;她對人生的看法已形成。有時她似乎較為贊成,我們通信。不過有一次,她退還我的信,說她覺得必須放下接受我的所有念頭。

passages.original: Professor and Mrs. Dennis took me from Cresson to their own home in New York, as soon as I could be removed, and I lay there some time under the former's personal supervision. Miss Whitfield called to see me, for I had written her the first words from Cresson I was able to write. She saw now that I needed her. I was left alone in the world. Now she could be in every sense the "helpmeet." Both her heart and head were now willing and the day was fixed. We were married in New York April 22, 1887, and sailed for our honeymoon which was passed on the Isle of Wight.
passages.vernacular: 我一能夠被移動,丹尼斯教授夫婦就將我從克雷森接到佢哋紐約嘅家,我喺嗰度躺咗一段時間,由前者親自照料。惠特菲爾德小姐嚟探望我,因為我從克雷森寫畀佢我能寫嘅第一句話。佢而家睇到我需要佢。我被留在世上孤身一人。而家佢可以喺各方面成為「伴侶」。佢嘅心同頭腦而家都願意,日子訂下喇。我哋於1887年4月22日喺紐約結婚,並啟航度蜜月,喺懷特島度過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一能夠被移動,丹尼斯教授夫婦就將我從克雷森接到他們紐約的家,我在那裡躺了一段時間,由前者親自照料。惠特菲爾德小姐來探望我,因為我從克雷森寫給她我能寫的第一句話。她現在看到我需要她。我被留在世上孤身一人。現在她可以在各方面成為「伴侶」。她的心和頭腦現在都願意,日子訂下了。我們於1887年4月22日在紐約結婚,並啟航度蜜月,在懷特島度過。

passages.original: (ABOUT 1878)]

Her delight was intense in finding the wild flowers. She had read of Wandering Willie, Heartsease, Forget-me-nots, the Primrose, Wild Thyme, and the whole list of homely names that had been to her only names till now. Everything charmed her. Uncle Lauder and one of my cousins came down from Scotland and visited us, and then we soon followed to the residence at Kilgraston they had selected for us in which to spend the summer. Scotland captured her. There was no doubt about that. Her girlish reading had been of Scotland--Scott's novels and "Scottish Chiefs" being her favorites. She soon became more Scotch than I. All this was fulfilling my fondest dreams.
passages.vernacular: 佢發現野花時喜悅強烈。佢讀過流浪嘅威利、三色堇、勿忘我、櫻草、野百里香,以及所有質樸名字嘅整張清單,呢啲名字直到而家對佢只係名字。一切都令佢著迷。勞德叔叔同我嘅一位表哥從蘇格蘭下嚟探我哋,然後我哋好快跟隨,到佢哋為我哋選好嘅基爾格拉斯頓住所度夏。蘇格蘭俘虜咗佢。這點毫無疑問。佢少女時代嘅閱讀係關於蘇格蘭——司各特嘅小說同《蘇格蘭酋長》係佢最愛。佢好快比我更蘇格蘭。所有呢一切都實現住我最深嘅夢想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她發現野花時喜悅強烈。她讀過流浪的威利、三色堇、勿忘我、櫻草、野百里香,以及所有質樸名字的整張清單,這些名字直到現在對她只是名字。一切都使她著迷。勞德叔叔和我的一位表哥從蘇格蘭下來探我們,然後我們很快跟隨,到他們為我們選好的基爾格拉斯頓住所度夏。蘇格蘭俘虜了她。這點毫無疑問。她少女時代的閱讀是關於蘇格蘭——司各特的小說和《蘇格蘭酋長》是她最愛。她很快比我更蘇格蘭。所有這一切都實現著我最深的夢想。

passages.original: We spent some days in Dunfermline and enjoyed them much. The haunts and incidents of my boyhood were visited and recited to her by all and sundry. She got nothing but flattering accounts of her husband which gave me a good start with her.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺鄧弗姆林度過幾天,非常享受。我童年嘅出沒之地同事件被所有人逐一參觀並講述畀佢聽。佢聽到嘅全係對佢丈夫嘅恭維,呢畀咗我一個好嘅開始。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在鄧弗姆林度過幾天,非常享受。我童年的出沒之地和事件被所有人逐一參觀並講述給她聽。她聽到的全是對她丈夫的恭維,這給了我一個好的開始。

passages.original: I was presented with the Freedom of Edinburgh as we passed northward--Lord Rosebery making the speech. The crowd in Edinburgh was great. I addressed the working-men in the largest hall and received a present from them as did Mrs. Carnegie also--a brooch she values highly. She heard and saw the pipers in all their glory and begged there should be one at our home--a piper to walk around and waken us in the morning and also to play us in to dinner. American as she is to the core, and Connecticut Puritan at that, she declared that if condemned to live upon a lonely island and allowed to choose only one musical instrument, it would be the pipes. The piper was secured quickly enough. One called and presented credentials from Cluny McPherson. We engaged him and were preceded by him playing the pipes as we entered our Kilgraston house.
passages.vernacular: 我哋北上時,我獲授予愛丁堡自由市民權——羅斯伯里勳爵致辭。愛丁堡人群眾多。我喺最大嘅禮堂向工人演講,並從佢哋嗰度得到一份禮物,卡內基夫人都一樣——一枚佢十分珍視嘅胸針。佢聽到並睇到風笛手嘅全部榮耀,懇求我哋家要有一位——一位風笛手,朝早走嚟走去喚醒我哋,並喺晚餐時奏樂引我哋入席。佢徹頭徹尾係美國人,仲係康涅狄格清教徒,卻宣稱如果被判處住喺孤島、只准選一件樂器,就選風笛。風笛手好快就找到喇。一位嚟訪,呈上克盧尼·麥克弗森嘅介紹信。我哋聘請咗佢,我哋進入基爾格拉斯頓住所時,佢喺前面吹奏風笛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們北上時,我獲授予愛丁堡自由市民權——羅斯伯里勳爵致辭。愛丁堡人群眾多。我在最大的禮堂向工人演講,並從他們那裡得到一份禮物,卡內基夫人也一樣——一枚她十分珍視的胸針。她聽到並看到風笛手的全部榮耀,懇求我們家要有一位——一位風笛手,早上走來走去喚醒我們,並在晚餐時奏樂引我們入席。她徹頭徹尾是美國人,還是康涅狄格清教徒,卻宣稱如果被判處住在孤島、只准選一件樂器,就選風笛。風笛手很快就找到了。一位來訪,呈上克盧尼·麥克弗森的介紹信。我們聘請了他,我們進入基爾格拉斯頓住所時,他在前面吹奏風笛。

passages.original: We enjoyed Kilgraston, although Mrs. Carnegie still longed for a wilder and more Highland home. Matthew Arnold visited us, as did Mr. and Mrs. Blaine, Senator and Mrs. Eugene Hale, and many friends. Mrs. Carnegie would have my relatives up from Dunfermline, especially the older uncles and aunties. She charmed every one. They expressed their surprise to me that she ever married me, but I told them I was equally surprised. The match had evidently been predestined.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喜歡基爾格拉斯頓,雖然卡內基夫人仍渴望更荒野、更高地嘅家。馬修·阿諾德探訪我哋,布萊恩夫婦、尤金·黑爾參議員夫婦同許多朋友都一樣。卡內基夫人會請我嘅親戚從鄧弗姆林上嚟,特別係年長嘅叔伯姨媽。佢迷倒每一個人。佢哋向我表示驚訝佢竟然嫁畀我,我告訴佢哋我同樣驚訝。呢門親事顯然係命中注定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們喜歡基爾格拉斯頓,雖然卡內基夫人仍渴望更荒野、更高地的家。馬修·阿諾德探訪我們,布萊恩夫婦、尤金·黑爾參議員夫婦和許多朋友也一樣。卡內基夫人會請我的親戚從鄧弗姆林上來,特別是年長的叔伯姨媽。她迷倒每一個人。他們向我表示驚訝她竟然嫁給我,我告訴他們我同樣驚訝。這門親事顯然是命中注定。

passages.original: We took our piper with us when we returned to New York, and also our housekeeper and some of the servants. Mrs. Nicoll remains with us still and is now, after twenty years' faithful service, as a member of the family. George Irvine, our butler, came to us a year later and is also as one of us. Maggie Anderson, one of the servants, is the same. They are devoted people, of high character and true loyalty.
passages.vernacular: 我哋返紐約時帶住風笛手,仲有管家同一些傭人。尼科爾太太仍然同我哋喺一起,而家經過二十年忠實服務,如同家人。我哋嘅管事喬治·歐文一年後來到我哋呢度,都如同我哋之一。傭人之一瑪姬·安德森都一樣。佢哋係忠心嘅人,品格高尚,真正忠誠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們回紐約時帶著風笛手,還有管家和一些傭人。尼科爾太太仍然與我們在一起,現在經過二十年忠實服務,如同家人。我們的管事喬治·歐文一年後來到我們這裡,也如同我們之一。傭人之一瑪姬·安德森也一樣。他們是忠心的人,品格高尚,真正忠誠。

passages.original: The next year we were offered and took Cluny Castle. Our piper was just the man to tell us all about it. He had been born and bred there and perhaps influenced our selection of that residence where we spent several summers.
passages.vernacular: 翌年我哋獲提供並租下克盧尼城堡。我哋嘅風笛手正是講述其一切嘅人。佢喺嗰度出生長大,或者影響咗我哋選擇嗰處住所,我哋喺嗰度度過幾個夏天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 翌年我們獲提供並租下克盧尼城堡。我們的風笛手正是講述其一切的人。他在那裡出生長大,也許影響了我們選擇那處住所,我們在那裡度過幾個夏天。

passages.original: On March 30, 1897, there came to us our daughter. As I first gazed upon her Mrs. Carnegie said,
passages.vernacular: 1897年3月30日,我哋嘅女兒到來。我第一次凝視佢時,卡內基夫人講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 1897年3月30日,我們的女兒到來。我第一次凝視她時,卡內基夫人說,

passages.original: "Her name is Margaret after your mother. Now one request I have to make."
passages.vernacular: 「佢叫瑪格麗特,以你母親命名。而家我有一個請求。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她叫瑪格麗特,以你母親命名。現在我有一個請求。」

passages.original: "What is it, Lou?"
passages.vernacular: 「係乜嘢,盧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是什麼,盧?」

passages.original: "We must get a summer home since this little one has been given us. We cannot rent one and be obliged to go in and go out at a certain date. It should be our home."
passages.vernacular: 「既然賜畀我哋呢個小寶貝,我哋必須有一個夏季嘅家。我哋唔能夠租一個,被迫喺某個日期搬進搬出。佢應該係我哋嘅家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「既然賜給我們這個小寶貝,我們必須有一個夏季的家。我們不能租一個,被迫在某個日期搬進搬出。它應該是我們的家。」

passages.original: "Yes," I agreed.
passages.vernacular: 「好,」我同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,」我同意。

passages.original: "I make only one condition."
passages.vernacular: 「我只有一個條件。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只有一個條件。」

passages.original: "What is that?" I asked.
passages.vernacular: 「係乜嘢?」我問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是什麼?」我問。

passages.original: "It must be in the Highlands of Scotland."
passages.vernacular: 「必須喺蘇格蘭高地。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「必須在蘇格蘭高地。」

passages.original: "Bless you," was my reply. "That suits me. You know I have to keep out of the sun's rays, and where can we do that so surely as among the heather? I'll be a committee of one to inquire and report."
passages.vernacular: 「祝福你,」係我嘅回答。「呢正合我意。你知道我必須避開陽光,而喺邊度能比喺石南叢中更肯定做到?我會做一人委員會去查詢同報告。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「祝福你,」是我的回答。「這正合我意。你知道我必須避開陽光,而在哪裡能比在石南叢中更肯定做到?我會做一人委員會去查詢和報告。」

passages.original: Skibo Castle was the result.
passages.vernacular: 結果就係斯基伯城堡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果就是斯基伯城堡。

passages.original: It is now twenty years since Mrs. Carnegie entered and changed my life, a few months after the passing of my mother and only brother left me alone in the world. My life has been made so happy by her that I cannot imagine myself living without her guardianship. I thought I knew her when she stood Ferdinand's test, but it was only the surface of her qualities I had seen and felt. Of their purity, holiness, wisdom, I had not sounded the depth. In every emergency of our active, changing, and in later years somewhat public life, in all her relations with others, including my family and her own, she has proved the diplomat and peace-maker. Peace and good-will attend her footsteps wherever her blessed influence extends. In the rare instances demanding heroic action it is she who first realizes this and plays the part.
passages.vernacular: 卡內基夫人進入並改變我嘅生活,至今已二十年,係喺我母親同唯一兄弟去世、留我孤身一人幾個月之後。佢令我嘅生活如此快樂,我無法想像自己冇佢嘅守護而生活。我以為我認識佢,當佢通過費迪南嘅考驗時,不過我睇到並感受到嘅只係佢品質嘅表面。佢嘅純潔、神聖、智慧,我未曾測出其深度。在我們活躍、多變、晚年有些公開的生活的每次緊急情況中,在她與他人的所有關係中,包括我的家人和她自己的家人,她已證明是外交家和和平締造者。無論佢有福嘅影響延伸到邊度,和平同善意都伴隨佢嘅腳步。喺罕見需要英雄行動嘅情況下,佢係第一個意識到並扮演角色嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卡內基夫人進入並改變我的生活,至今已二十年,是在我母親和唯一兄弟去世、留我孤身一人幾個月之後。她使我的生活如此快樂,我無法想像自己沒有她的守護而生活。我以為我認識她,當她通過費迪南的考驗時,不過我看到並感受到的只是她品質的表面。她的純潔、神聖、智慧,我未曾測出其深度。在我們活躍、多變、晚年有些公開的生活的每次緊急情況中,在她與他人的所有關係中,包括我的家人和她自己的家人,她已證明是外交家和和平締造者。無論她有福的影響延伸到哪裡,和平與善意都伴隨她的腳步。在罕見需要英雄行動的情況下,她是第一個意識到並扮演角色的人。

passages.original: The Peace-Maker has never had a quarrel in all her life, not even with a schoolmate, and there does not live a soul upon the earth who has met her who has the slightest cause to complain of neglect. Not that she does not welcome the best and gently avoid the undesirable--none is more fastidious than she--but neither rank, wealth, nor social position affects her one iota. She is incapable of acting or speaking rudely; all is in perfect good taste. Still, she never lowers the standard. Her intimates are only of the best. She is always thinking how she can do good to those around her--planning for this one and that in case of need and making such judicious arrangements or presents as surprise those coöperating with her.
passages.vernacular: 呢位和平締造者一生從未有過爭吵,甚至同同學都冇,世上冇一個遇見過佢嘅人,有絲毫理由抱怨被忽視。並非佢不歡迎最好嘅人、不溫和避開不受歡迎嘅人——沒人比佢更挑剔——但地位、財富、社會身分都絲毫不影響佢。佢無法無禮地行事或講話;一切都極有品味。然而佢從不降低標準。佢嘅知己只有最好嘅。佢總是喺想點樣對周圍嘅人行善——為呢個同嗰個人喺需要時計劃,並作出明智安排或贈禮,令同佢合作嘅人驚喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位和平締造者一生從未有過爭吵,甚至與同學都沒有,世上沒有一個遇見過她的人,有絲毫理由抱怨被忽視。並非她不歡迎最好的人、不溫和避開不受歡迎的人——沒人比她更挑剔——但地位、財富、社會身分都絲毫不影響她。她無法無禮地行事或說話;一切都極有品味。然而她從不降低標準。她的知己只有最好的。她總是在想怎樣對周圍的人行善——為這個和那個人在需要時計劃,並作出明智安排或贈禮,使與她合作的人驚喜。

passages.original: I cannot imagine myself going through these twenty years without her. Nor can I endure the thought of living after her. In the course of nature I have not that to meet; but then the thought of what will be cast upon her, a woman left alone with so much requiring attention and needing a man to decide, gives me intense pain and I sometimes wish I had this to endure for her. But then she will have our blessed daughter in her life and perhaps that will keep her patient. Besides, Margaret needs her more than she does her father.
passages.vernacular: 我無法想像自己冇佢而度過呢二十年。我都無法忍受喺佢之後生活嘅念頭。按自然規律,我唔使面對嗰個;但想到將落喺佢身上嘅,一個被留下獨自面對咁多需要關注、需要男人決定嘅事嘅女人,畀我劇烈痛苦,我有時希望我為佢承受呢個。不過佢生命中會有我哋有福嘅女兒,或者嗰會使佢有耐性。此外,瑪格麗特比需要父親更需要佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我無法想像自己沒有她而度過這二十年。我也無法忍受在她之後生活的念頭。按自然規律,我不必面對那個;但想到將落在她身上的,一個被留下獨自面對這麼多需要關注、需要男人決定的事的女人,給我劇烈痛苦,我有時希望我為她承受這個。不過她生命中會有我們有福的女兒,也許那會使她有耐性。此外,瑪格麗特比需要父親更需要她。

passages.original: Why, oh, why, are we compelled to leave the heaven we have found on earth and go we know not where! For I can say with Jessica:
passages.vernacular: 點解,哦點解,我哋被迫離開在世上找到嘅天堂,去往我哋唔知道嘅地方!因為我可以同傑西卡一起講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼,哦為什麼,我們被迫離開在世上找到的天堂,去往我們不知道的地方!因為我可以和傑西卡一起說:

passages.original: "It is very meet The Lord Bassanio live an upright life; For, having such a blessing in his lady, He finds the joys of heaven here on earth."
passages.vernacular: 「巴薩尼奧主人過正直嘅生活係好合宜嘅;因為擁有咁樣嘅福氣喺佢夫人身上,佢喺呢世上就找到天堂嘅喜悅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巴薩尼奧主人過正直的生活是很合宜的;因為擁有這樣的福氣在他夫人身上,他在這世上就找到天堂的喜悅。」

chapters.title: Mills and the Men 工廠與工人

passages.original: The one vital lesson in iron and steel that I learned in Britain was the necessity for owning raw materials and finishing the completed article ready for its purpose. Having solved the steel-rail problem at the Edgar Thomson Works, we soon proceeded to the next step. The difficulties and uncertainties of obtaining regular supplies of pig iron compelled us to begin the erection of blast furnaces. Three of these were built, one, however, being a reconstructed blast furnace purchased from the Escanaba Iron Company, with which Mr. Kloman had been connected. As is usual in such cases, the furnace cost us as much as a new one, and it never was as good. There is nothing so unsatisfactory as purchases of inferior plants.
passages.vernacular: 我喺英國學到有關鋼鐵嘅唯一關鍵教訓,就係必須擁有原料,並將製成品做到可以即刻使用。喺埃德加·湯姆森工廠解決咗鋼軌問題之後,我哋好快就進行下一步。要穩定取得生鐵供應,既困難又不確定,迫使我哋開始興建高爐。一共建咗三座,不過其中一座係從埃斯卡納巴鐵業公司(克洛曼先生曾與之有關)買嚟重建嘅高爐。同往常一樣,呢座爐花嘅錢同新爐一樣多,但從來冇新爐咁好。冇乜比買次等工廠更令人失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在英國學到有關鋼鐵的唯一關鍵教訓,就是必須擁有原料,並將製成品做到可以立即使用。在埃德加·湯姆森工廠解決了鋼軌問題之後,我們很快就進行下一步。要穩定取得生鐵供應,既困難又不確定,迫使我們開始興建高爐。一共建了三座,不過其中一座是從埃斯卡納巴鐵業公司(克洛曼先生曾與之有關)買來重建的高爐。和往常一樣,這座爐花的錢和新爐一樣多,但從來沒新爐那麼好。沒什麼比買次等工廠更令人失望。

passages.original: But although this purchase was a mistake, directly considered, it proved, at a subsequent date, a source of great profit because it gave us a furnace small enough for the manufacture of spiegel and, at a later date, of ferro-manganese. We were the second firm in the United States to manufacture our own spiegel, and the first, and for years the only, firm in America that made ferro-manganese. We had been dependent upon foreigners for a supply of this indispensable article, paying as high as eighty dollars a ton for it. The manager of our blast furnaces, Mr. Julian Kennedy, is entitled to the credit of suggesting that with the ores within reach we could make ferro-manganese in our small furnace. The experiment was worth trying and the result was a great success. We were able to supply the entire American demand and prices fell from eighty to fifty dollars per ton as a consequence.
passages.vernacular: 不過雖然直接嚟睇,呢次購買係錯誤,後來卻證明係巨額利潤嘅來源,因為佢畀咗我哋一座細到可以製造鏡鐵,後來亦可製造錳鐵嘅高爐。我哋係美國第二間自己製造鏡鐵嘅公司,亦係美國第一間、而且多年來唯一一間製造錳鐵嘅公司。我哋以前要靠外國人供應呢種不可或缺嘅物品,每噸要付到八十元。我哋高爐經理朱利安·肯尼迪先生,功勞在於提出憑我哋能夠取得嘅礦石,可以喺我哋嗰座細爐製造錳鐵。呢個實驗值得一試,結果大獲成功。我哋能夠供應整個美國嘅需求,價格因此由每噸八十元跌到五十元。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過雖然直接來看,這次購買是錯誤,後來卻證明是巨額利潤的來源,因為它給了我們一座小到可以製造鏡鐵,後來也可製造錳鐵的高爐。我們是美國第二間自己製造鏡鐵的公司,也是美國第一間、而且多年來唯一一間製造錳鐵的公司。我們以前要靠外國人供應這種不可或缺的物品,每噸要付到八十元。我們高爐經理朱利安·肯尼迪先生,功勞在於提出憑我們能夠取得的礦石,可以在我們那座小爐製造錳鐵。這個實驗值得一試,結果大獲成功。我們能夠供應整個美國的需求,價格因此由每噸八十元跌到五十元。

passages.original: While testing the ores of Virginia we found that these were being quietly purchased by Europeans for ferro-manganese, the owners of the mine being led to believe that they were used for other purposes. Our Mr. Phipps at once set about purchasing that mine. He obtained an option from the owners, who had neither capital nor skill to work it efficiently. A high price was paid to them for their interests, and (with one of them, Mr. Davis, a very able young man) we became the owners, but not until a thorough investigation of the mine had proved that there was enough of manganese ore in sight to repay us. All this was done with speed; not a day was lost when the discovery was made. And here lies the great advantage of a partnership over a corporation. The president of the latter would have had to consult a board of directors and wait several weeks and perhaps months for their decision. By that time the mine would probably have become the property of others.
passages.vernacular: 測試維珍尼亞礦石時,我哋發現歐洲人正悄悄購買呢啲礦石來製造錳鐵,礦場東主被引導相信佢哋用於其他目的。我哋嘅菲普斯先生即刻著手收購嗰個礦場。佢從東主處取得選擇權,東主既冇資本亦冇技術有效開採。我哋付咗高價買佢哋嘅權益,並(同其中一位戴維斯先生,一個好有能力嘅年輕人)成為業主,但要等徹底調查礦場,證明眼前有足夠嘅錳礦石回報我哋先至。所有呢啲都做得好快;發現礦場後一日都冇浪費。呢度就係合夥比公司嘅最大好處。公司總裁要諮詢董事會,等幾個星期甚至幾個月先有決定。到嗰時,礦場大概已經成為他人嘅財產。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 測試維珍尼亞礦石時,我們發現歐洲人正悄悄購買這些礦石來製造錳鐵,礦場東主被引導相信它們用於其他目的。我們的菲普斯先生立刻著手收購那個礦場。他從東主處取得選擇權,東主既沒資本也沒技術有效開採。我們付了高價買他們的權益,並(與其中一位戴維斯先生,一個很有能力的年輕人)成為業主,但要等徹底調查礦場,證明眼前有足夠的錳礦石回報我們才行。所有這些都做得很快;發現礦場後一天都沒浪費。這裡就是合夥比公司的最大好處。公司總裁要諮詢董事會,等幾個星期甚至幾個月才有決定。到那時,礦場大概已經成為他人的財產。

passages.original: We continued to develop our blast-furnace plant, every new one being a great improvement upon the preceding, until at last we thought we had arrived at a standard furnace. Minor improvements would no doubt be made, but so far as we could see we had a perfect plant and our capacity was then fifty thousand tons per month of pig iron.
passages.vernacular: 我哋繼續發展高爐設施,每一座新嘅都比前一座大有改進,直到最後我哋認為已經造出一座標準高爐。小改進無疑還會有,不過就我哋所見,我哋已有完美嘅設施,當時產能係每月五萬噸生鐵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們繼續發展高爐設施,每一座新的都比前一座大有改進,直到最後我們認為已經造出一座標準高爐。小改進無疑還會有,不過就我們所見,我們已有完美的設施,當時產能是每月五萬噸生鐵。

passages.original: The blast-furnace department was no sooner added than another step was seen to be essential to our independence and success. The supply of superior coke was a fixed quantity--the Connellsville field being defined. We found that we could not get on without a supply of the fuel essential to the smelting of pig iron; and a very thorough investigation of the question led us to the conclusion that the Frick Coke Company had not only the best coal and coke property, but that it had in Mr. Frick himself a man with a positive genius for its management. He had proved his ability by starting as a poor railway clerk and succeeding. In 1882 we purchased one half of the stock of this company, and by subsequent purchases from other holders we became owners of the great bulk of the shares.
passages.vernacular: 高爐部門剛加入,就見到另一步對我哋嘅獨立同成功係必不可少。優質焦炭嘅供應係固定數量——康奈爾斯維爾礦區是有界限的。我哋發現冇熔煉生鐵必需嘅燃料供應就搞唔掂;非常徹底調查此問題後,我哋斷定弗里克焦炭公司唔單止擁有最好嘅煤同焦炭資產,而且在弗里克先生本人身上有一個對管理有絕對天賦嘅人。佢由貧窮嘅鐵路文員開始並成功,證明咗佢嘅能力。1882年我哋購買咗該公司一半股票,之後向其他持有人購買,我哋成為大部分股份嘅業主。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高爐部門剛加入,就看到另一步對我們的獨立和成功是必不可少。優質焦炭的供應是固定數量——康奈爾斯維爾礦區是有界限的。我們發現沒熔煉生鐵必需的燃料供應就搞不定;非常徹底調查此問題後,我們斷定弗里克焦炭公司不僅擁有最好的煤和焦炭資產,而且在弗里克先生本人身上有一個對管理有絕對天賦的人。他由貧窮的鐵路文員開始並成功,證明了他的能力。1882年我們購買了該公司一半股票,之後向其他持有人購買,我們成為大部分股份的業主。

passages.original: There now remained to be acquired only the supply of iron stone. If we could obtain this we should be in the position occupied by only two or three of the European concerns. We thought at one time we had succeeded in discovering in Pennsylvania this last remaining link in the chain. We were misled, however, in our investment in the Tyrone region, and lost considerable sums as the result of our attempts to mine and use the ores of that section. They promised well at the edges of the mines, where the action of the weather for ages had washed away impurities and enriched the ore, but when we penetrated a small distance they proved too "lean" to work.
passages.vernacular: 而家只剩低鐵礦石供應有待取得。如果我哋取得這個,我哋就會處於只有兩三間歐洲公司佔據嘅位置。我哋一度以為在賓夕法尼亞發現咗鏈條上最後剩低嘅一環。不過我哋在泰隆地區嘅投資被誤導,嘗試開採使用該地區礦石,損失相當金額。佢哋在礦場邊緣前景良好,嗰度多年風化沖走雜質,令礦石變豐富,不過我哋深入少少,就證明太「貧」無法開採。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在只剩下鐵礦石供應有待取得。如果我們取得這個,我們就會處於只有兩三間歐洲公司佔據的位置。我們一度以為在賓夕法尼亞發現了鏈條上最後剩下的一環。不過我們在泰隆地區的投資被誤導,嘗試開採使用該地區礦石,損失相當金額。它們在礦場邊緣前景良好,那裡多年風化沖走雜質,使礦石變豐富,不過我們深入一點,就證明太「貧」無法開採。

passages.original: Our chemist, Mr. Prousser, was then sent to a Pennsylvania furnace among the hills which we had leased, with instructions to analyze all the materials brought to him from the district, and to encourage people to bring him specimens of minerals. A striking example of the awe inspired by the chemist in those days was that only with great difficulty could he obtain a man or a boy to assist him in the laboratory. He was suspected of illicit intercourse with the Powers of Evil when he undertook to tell by his suspicious-looking apparatus what a stone contained. I believe that at last we had to send him a man from our office at Pittsburgh.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅化學家普魯瑟先生當時被派去我哋租下嘅山間一座賓夕法尼亞高爐,指示佢分析該地區帶畀佢嘅所有物料,並鼓勵人們帶礦物標本畀佢。當時化學家令人敬畏嘅一個明顯例子,係佢好難先找到一個男人或男孩在實驗室幫手。佢被懷疑與邪惡力量有非法來往,因為佢憑可疑嘅儀器講出石頭含有咩。我相信最後我哋要從匹茲堡辦公室派一個人畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的化學家普魯瑟先生當時被派去我們租下的山間一座賓夕法尼亞高爐,指示他分析該地區帶給他的所有物料,並鼓勵人們帶礦物標本給他。當時化學家令人敬畏的一個明顯例子,是他好難才找到一個男人或男孩在實驗室幫手。他被懷疑與邪惡力量有非法來往,因為他憑可疑的儀器說出石頭含有什麼。我相信最後我們要從匹茲堡辦公室派一個人給他。

passages.original: One day he sent us a report of analyses of ore remarkable for the absence of phosphorus. It was really an ore suitable for making Bessemer steel. Such a discovery attracted our attention at once. The owner of the property was Moses Thompson, a rich farmer, proprietor of seven thousand acres of the most beautiful agricultural land in Center County, Pennsylvania. An appointment was made to meet him upon the ground from which the ore had been obtained. We found the mine had been worked for a charcoal blast furnace fifty or sixty years before, but it had not borne a good reputation then, the reason no doubt being that its product was so much purer than other ores that the same amount of flux used caused trouble in smelting. It was so good it was good for nothing in those days of old.
passages.vernacular: 有一日佢寄畀我哋一份礦石分析報告,顯著之處係冇磷。真係一種適合製造貝塞麥鋼嘅礦石。呢個發現即刻引起我哋注意。產業業主係摩西·湯普森,富有農夫,擁有賓夕法尼亞州中心縣七千英畝最美麗農地。約定在礦石來源嘅地方與佢見面。我哋發現礦場五六十年前曾為木炭高爐開採,不過當時名聲唔好,原因無疑係其產品比其他礦石純得多,用同樣份量嘅熔劑造成熔煉麻煩。佢好到喺舊日一無是處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天他寄給我們一份礦石分析報告,顯著之處是沒磷。真是一種適合製造貝塞麥鋼的礦石。這個發現立刻引起我們注意。產業業主是摩西·湯普森,富有農夫,擁有賓夕法尼亞州中心縣七千英畝最美麗農地。約定在礦石來源的地方與他見面。我們發現礦場五六十年前曾為木炭高爐開採,不過當時名聲不好,原因無疑是其產品比其他礦石純得多,用同樣份量的熔劑造成熔煉麻煩。它好到在舊日一無是處。

passages.original: We finally obtained the right to take the mine over at any time within six months, and we therefore began the work of examination, which every purchaser of mineral property should make most carefully. We ran lines across the hillside fifty feet apart, with cross-lines at distances of a hundred feet apart, and at each point of intersection we put a shaft down through the ore. I believe there were eighty such shafts in all and the ore was analyzed at every few feet of depth, so that before we paid over the hundred thousand dollars asked we knew exactly what there was of ore. The result hoped for was more than realized. Through the ability of my cousin and partner, Mr. Lauder, the cost of mining and washing was reduced to a low figure, and the Scotia ore made good all the losses we had incurred in the other mines, paid for itself, and left a profit besides. In this case, at least, we snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. We trod upon sure ground with the chemist as our guide. It will be seen that we were determined to get raw materials and were active in the pursuit.
passages.vernacular: 我哋終於取得六個月內隨時接管礦場嘅權利,所以開始檢查工作,每個購買礦產嘅人都應該最仔細咁做。我哋喺山坡拉線,每條相隔五十呎,橫線相隔一百呎,每個交叉點穿過礦石掘一個豎井。我相信一共有八十個豎井,礦石每隔幾呎深度都作分析,所以在付出所要求嘅十萬元之前,我哋確切知道有幾多礦石。所希望嘅結果還超額實現。憑我表哥兼合夥人勞德先生嘅能力,開採同洗礦成本降到低水平,蘇格蒂亞礦石彌補咗我哋在其他礦場招致嘅所有損失,自己賺回成本,仲留低利潤。至少在這個個案,我哋從失敗口中搶得勝利。有化學家作嚮導,我哋踏在穩固嘅地面上。可見我哋決心取得原料,並積極追求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們終於取得六個月內隨時接管礦場的權利,所以開始檢查工作,每個購買礦產的人都應該最仔細地做。我們在山坡拉線,每條相隔五十呎,橫線相隔一百呎,每個交叉點穿過礦石掘一個豎井。我相信一共有八十個豎井,礦石每隔幾呎深度都作分析,所以在付出所要求的十萬元之前,我們確切知道有多少礦石。所希望的結果還超額實現。憑我表哥兼合夥人勞德先生的能力,開採和洗礦成本降到低水平,蘇格蒂亞礦石彌補了我們在其他礦場招致的所有損失,自己賺回成本,還留下利潤。至少在這個個案,我們從失敗口中搶得勝利。有化學家作嚮導,我們踏在穩固的地面上。可見我們決心取得原料,並積極追求。

passages.original: We had lost and won, but the escapes in business affairs are sometimes very narrow. Driving with Mr. Phipps from the mills one day we passed the National Trust Company office on Penn Street, Pittsburgh. I noticed the large gilt letters across the window, "Stockholders individually liable." That very morning in looking over a statement of our affairs I had noticed twenty shares "National Trust Company" on the list of assets. I said to Harry:
passages.vernacular: 我哋有輸有贏,但商業事務嘅逃脫有時非常驚險。有一日同菲普斯先生從工廠駕車,我哋經過匹茲堡賓夕街嘅國民信託公司辦公室。我留意到窗口上巨大鍍金字母:「股東須個別負責」。嗰日朝早,我睇我哋事務報表時,留意到資產清單上有二十股「國民信託公司」。我對哈利講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們有輸有贏,但商業事務的逃脫有時非常驚險。有一天與菲普斯先生從工廠駕車,我們經過匹茲堡賓街的國民信託公司辦公室。我留意到窗口上巨大鍍金字母:「股東須個別負責」。那天早上,我看我們事務報表時,留意到資產清單上有二十股「國民信託公司」。我對哈利說:

passages.original: "If this is the concern we own shares in, won't you please sell them before you return to the office this afternoon?"
passages.vernacular: 「如果這就是我哋有股份嘅公司,你今日下午返辦公室前,可唔可以賣咗佢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果這就是我們有股份的公司,你今天下午回辦公室前,可不可以賣了它?」

passages.original: He saw no need for haste. It would be done in good time.
passages.vernacular: 佢見唔到有需要趕。好快就會做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看不到有需要趕。很快就會做。

passages.original: "No, Harry, oblige me by doing it instantly."
passages.vernacular: 「唔,哈利,請你幫我即刻做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,哈利,請你幫我立刻做。」

passages.original: He did so and had it transferred. Fortunate, indeed, was this, for in a short time the bank failed with an enormous deficit. My cousin, Mr. Morris, was among the ruined shareholders. Many others met the same fate. Times were panicky, and had we been individually liable for all the debts of the National Trust Company our credit would inevitably have been seriously imperiled. It was a narrow escape. And with only twenty shares (two thousand dollars' worth of stock), taken to oblige friends who wished our name on their list of shareholders! The lesson was not lost. The sound rule in business is that you may give money freely when you have a surplus, but your name never--neither as endorser nor as member of a corporation with individual liability. A trifling investment of a few thousand dollars, a mere trifle--yes, but a trifle possessed of deadly explosive power.
passages.vernacular: 佢照做並辦理轉讓。確實幸運,因為不久銀行倒閉,留下巨額赤字。我表哥莫里斯先生係受災股東之一。許多其他人遭遇同樣命運。時局恐慌,如果我哋要為國民信託公司所有債務個別負責,我哋嘅信用必然會受到嚴重威脅。係驚險逃脫。而且只係二十股(價值二千元股票),是為幫想在股東名單上有我哋名字的朋友而買!教訓冇白費。商業上嘅健全規則係:你有盈餘時可以慷慨畀錢,但你嘅名字永遠不可以——不論作為背書人,仲係作為有個別責任嘅公司成員。幾千元微小投資,不過是小事——係,但是具有致命爆炸力的小事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他照做並辦理轉讓。確實幸運,因為不久銀行倒閉,留下巨額赤字。我表哥莫里斯先生是受災股東之一。許多其他人遭遇同樣命運。時局恐慌,如果我們要為國民信託公司所有債務個別負責,我們的信用必然會受到嚴重威脅。是驚險逃脫。而且只是二十股(價值二千元股票),是為幫想在股東名單上有我們名字的朋友而買!教訓沒有白費。商業上的健全規則是:你有盈餘時可以慷慨給錢,但你的名字永遠不可以——不論作為背書人,還是作為有個別責任的公司成員。幾千元微小投資,不過是小事——是,但是具有致命爆炸力的小事。

passages.original: The rapid substitution of steel for iron in the immediate future had become obvious to us. Even in our Keystone Bridge Works, steel was being used more and more in place of iron. King Iron was about to be deposed by the new King Steel, and we were becoming more and more dependent upon it. We had about concluded in 1886 to build alongside of the Edgar Thomson Mills new works for the manufacture of miscellaneous shapes of steel when it was suggested to us that the five or six leading manufacturers of Pittsburgh, who had combined to build steel mills at Homestead, were willing to sell their mills to us.
passages.vernacular: 不久將來鋼迅速取代鐵,對我哋已變得明顯。甚至在我哋基石橋樑工廠,鋼也越來越多取代鐵。鐵王即將被新鋼王罷黜,我哋越來越依賴它。1886年我哋差不多決定在埃德加·湯姆森工廠旁建造新廠製造各種形狀嘅鋼,這時有人向我哋建議,聯合起來在霍姆斯特德建鋼廠嘅匹茲堡五六位主要製造商,願意將佢哋嘅工廠賣畀我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久將來鋼迅速取代鐵,對我們已變得明顯。甚至在我們基石橋樑工廠,鋼也越來越多取代鐵。鐵王即將被新鋼王罷黜,我們越來越依賴它。1886年我們差不多決定在埃德加·湯姆森工廠旁建造新廠製造各種形狀的鋼,這時有人向我們建議,聯合起來在霍姆斯特德建鋼廠的匹茲堡五六位主要製造商,願意將他們的工廠賣給我們。

passages.original: These works had been built originally by a syndicate of manufacturers, with the view of obtaining the necessary supplies of steel which they required in their various concerns, but the steel-rail business, being then in one of its booms, they had been tempted to change plans and construct a steel-rail mill. They had been able to make rails as long as prices remained high, but, as the mills had not been specially designed for this purpose, they were without the indispensable blast furnaces for the supply of pig iron, and had no coke lands for the supply of fuel. They were in no condition to compete with us.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲工廠最初由一個製造商辛迪加建造,目的係取得佢哋各種企業所需嘅鋼供應,不過當時鋼軌業務正處於繁榮期,佢哋被誘惑改變計劃,建造鋼軌廠。只要價格保持高企,他們就能夠造軌,不過因為工廠並非為此特別設計,他們沒有供應生鐵必不可少嘅高爐,也沒有供應燃料的焦炭地。佢哋無法同我哋競爭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些工廠最初由一個製造商辛迪加建造,目的是取得他們各種企業所需的鋼供應,不過當時鋼軌業務正處於繁榮期,他們被誘惑改變計劃,建造鋼軌廠。只要價格保持高企,他們就能夠造軌,不過因為工廠並非為此特別設計,他們沒有供應生鐵必不可少的高爐,也沒有供應燃料的焦炭地。他們無法與我們競爭。

passages.original: It was advantageous for us to purchase these works. I felt there was only one way we could deal with their owners, and that was to propose a consolidation with Carnegie Brothers & Co. We offered to do so on equal terms, every dollar they had invested to rank against our dollars. Upon this basis the negotiation was promptly concluded. We, however, gave to all parties the option to take cash, and most fortunately for us, all elected to do so except Mr. George Singer, who continued with us to his and our entire satisfaction. Mr. Singer told us afterwards that his associates had been greatly exercised as to how they could meet the proposition I was to lay before them. They were much afraid of being overreached but when I proposed equality all around, dollar for dollar, they were speechless.
passages.vernacular: 購買呢啲工廠對我哋有利。我覺得我哋只有一個辦法對付佢哋嘅東主,就係提議與卡內基兄弟公司合併。我哋提出以平等條件合併,佢哋投入嘅每一元對應我哋每一元。喺呢基礎上談判迅速完成。不過我哋畀所有人選擇取現金,對我哋極為幸運嘅係,除咗喬治·辛格先生,所有人都選現金,辛格先生繼續與我哋合作,令他和我們都完全滿意。辛格先生後來告訴我哋,佢嘅同事曾極度煩惱點樣應對我要向佢哋提出嘅建議。佢哋好怕被佔便宜,不過當我提出一律平等、一元對一元,佢哋說不出話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 購買這些工廠對我們有利。我覺得我們只有一個辦法對付他們的東主,就是提議與卡內基兄弟公司合併。我們提出以平等條件合併,他們投入的每一元對應我們每一元。在這基礎上談判迅速完成。不過我們給所有人選擇取現金,對我們極為幸運的是,除了喬治·辛格先生,所有人都選現金,辛格先生繼續與我們合作,使他和我們都完全滿意。辛格先生後來告訴我們,他的同事曾極度煩惱怎樣應對我要向他們提出的建議。他們很怕被佔便宜,不過當我提出一律平等、一元對一元,他們說不出話。

passages.original: This purchase led to the reconstruction of all our firms. The new firm of Carnegie, Phipps & Co. was organized in 1886 to run the Homestead Mills. The firm of Wilson, Walker & Co. was embraced in the firm of Carnegie, Phipps & Co., Mr. Walker being elected chairman. My brother was chairman of Carnegie Brothers & Co. and at the head of all. A further extension of our business was the establishing of the Hartman Steel Works at Beaver Falls, designed to work into a hundred various forms the product of the Homestead Mills. So now we made almost everything in steel from a wire nail up to a twenty-inch steel girder, and it was then not thought probable that we should enter into any new field.
passages.vernacular: 這次購買導致我哋所有公司重組。新公司卡內基-菲普斯公司於1886年組織成立,經營霍姆斯特德工廠。威爾遜-沃克公司併入卡內基-菲普斯公司,沃克先生當選主席。我細佬係卡內基兄弟公司主席,位居所有人之首。業務進一步擴展係喺比弗瀑布建立哈特曼鋼廠,旨喺將霍姆斯特德工廠嘅產品加工成一百種不同形式。所以我哋現在幾乎製造所有鋼製品,從鋼釘到二十吋鋼樑,當時不認為我哋會進入任何新領域。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次購買導致我們所有公司重組。新公司卡內基-菲普斯公司於1886年組織成立,經營霍姆斯特德工廠。威爾遜-沃克公司併入卡內基-菲普斯公司,沃克先生當選主席。我弟弟是卡內基兄弟公司主席,位居所有人之首。業務進一步擴展是在比弗瀑布建立哈特曼鋼廠,旨在將霍姆斯特德工廠的產品加工成一百種不同形式。所以我們現在幾乎製造所有鋼製品,從鋼釘到二十吋鋼樑,當時不認為我們會進入任何新領域。

passages.original: It may be interesting here to note the progress of our works during the decade 1888 to 1897. In 1888 we had twenty millions of dollars invested; in 1897 more than double or over forty-five millions. The 600,000 tons of pig iron we made per annum in 1888 was trebled; we made nearly 2,000,000. Our product of iron and steel was in 1888, say, 2000 tons per day; it grew to exceed 6000 tons. Our coke works then embraced about 5000 ovens; they were trebled in number, and our capacity, then 6000 tons, became 18,000 tons per day. Our Frick Coke Company in 1897 had 42,000 acres of coal land, more than two thirds of the true Connellsville vein. Ten years hence increased production may be found to have been equally rapid. It may be accepted as an axiom that a manufacturing concern in a growing country like ours begins to decay when it stops extending.
passages.vernacular: 在這裡記下1888年至1897年十年間我哋工廠嘅進展,也許有趣。1888年我哋投資二千萬元;1897年多過一倍,超過四千五百萬元。1888年我哋每年製造嘅六十萬噸生鐵增加到三倍;我哋製造近二百萬噸。我哋鋼鐵產量1888年大約每日二千噸;增長到超過六千噸。我哋嘅煉焦廠當時有約五千座爐;數目增至三倍,產能由當時六千噸變成每日一萬八千噸。1897年我哋嘅弗里克焦炭公司有四萬二千英畝煤地,超過康奈爾斯維爾真正礦脈的三分之二。十年後可能會發現產量增加同樣迅速。可以接受為公理:在我哋這樣成長中國家的製造企業,一旦停止擴展就開始衰敗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡記下1888年至1897年十年間我們工廠的進展,也許有趣。1888年我們投資二千萬元;1897年多過一倍,超過四千五百萬元。1888年我們每年製造的六十萬噸生鐵增加到三倍;我們製造近二百萬噸。我們鋼鐵產量1888年大約每天二千噸;增長到超過六千噸。我們的煉焦廠當時有約五千座爐;數目增至三倍,產能由當時六千噸變成每天一萬八千噸。1897年我們的弗里克焦炭公司有四萬二千英畝煤地,超過康奈爾斯維爾真正礦脈的三分之二。十年後可能會發現產量增加同樣迅速。可以接受為公理:在我們這樣成長中國家的製造企業,一旦停止擴展就開始衰敗。

passages.original: To make a ton of steel one and a half tons of iron stone has to be mined, transported by rail a hundred miles to the Lakes, carried by boat hundreds of miles, transferred to cars, transported by rail one hundred and fifty miles to Pittsburgh; one and a half tons of coal must be mined and manufactured into coke and carried fifty-odd miles by rail; and one ton of limestone mined and carried one hundred and fifty miles to Pittsburgh. How then could steel be manufactured and sold without loss at three pounds for two cents? This, I confess, seemed to me incredible, and little less than miraculous, but it was so.
passages.vernacular: 要造一噸鋼,要開採一噸半鐵礦石,用鐵路運一百英里到湖區,用船運數百英里,轉到火車,再用鐵路運一百五十英里到匹茲堡;要開採一噸半煤並製成焦炭,用鐵路運五十多英里;仲要開採一噸石灰石,運一百五十英里到匹茲堡。咁鋼點樣能以三磅兩仙製造同出售而不虧本?我承認,呢喺我看來難以置信,近乎奇蹟,但事實如此。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要造一噸鋼,要開採一噸半鐵礦石,用鐵路運一百英里到湖區,用船運數百英里,轉到火車,再用鐵路運一百五十英里到匹茲堡;要開採一噸半煤並製成焦炭,用鐵路運五十多英里;還要開採一噸石灰石,運一百五十英里到匹茲堡。那麼鋼怎樣能以三磅兩仙製造和出售而不虧本?我承認,這在我看來難以置信,近乎奇蹟,但事實如此。

passages.original: America is soon to change from being the dearest steel manufacturing country to the cheapest. Already the shipyards of Belfast are our customers. This is but the beginning. Under present conditions America can produce steel as cheaply as any other land, notwithstanding its higher-priced labor. There is no labor so cheap as the dearest in the mechanical field, provided it is free, contented, zealous, and reaping reward as it renders service. And here America leads.
passages.vernacular: 美國不久將由最昂貴嘅鋼製造國變成最便宜嘅。貝爾法斯特的船廠已是我哋的客戶。呢只係開始。喺目前條件下,美國能以同任何其他國家一樣低嘅價格生產鋼,儘管勞工價格較高。機械領域冇勞工比最昂貴嘅更便宜,只要佢哋自由、滿足、熱心,並喺提供服務時得到回報。而在這點上美國領先。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美國不久將由最昂貴的鋼製造國變成最便宜的。貝爾法斯特的船廠已是我們的客戶。這只是開始。在目前條件下,美國能以和任何其他國家一樣低的價格生產鋼,儘管勞工價格較高。機械領域沒有勞工比最昂貴的更便宜,只要他們自由、滿足、熱心,並在提供服務時得到回報。而在這點上美國領先。

passages.original: One great advantage which America will have in competing in the markets of the world is that her manufacturers will have the best home market. Upon this they can depend for a return upon capital, and the surplus product can be exported with advantage, even when the prices received for it do not more than cover actual cost, provided the exports be charged with their proportion of all expenses. The nation that has the best home market, especially if products are standardized, as ours are, can soon outsell the foreign producer. The phrase I used in Britain in this connection was: "The Law of the Surplus." It afterward came into general use in commercial discussions.
passages.vernacular: 美國在世界市場競爭嘅一大優勢,係其製造商將擁有最好嘅國內市場。佢哋可以依靠佢取得資本回報,剩餘產品可以有利地出口,即使其所得價格僅足以覆蓋實際成本,只要出口分攤其所佔全部開支比例。擁有最好國內市場嘅國家,尤其係產品標準化(如我哋嘅),可以好快賣得比外國生產者更多。我喺英國就此使用嘅說法係:「剩餘定律」。佢後來喺商業討論中普遍使用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美國在世界市場競爭的一大優勢,是其製造商將擁有最好的國內市場。他們可以依靠它取得資本回報,剩餘產品可以有利地出口,即使其所得價格僅足以覆蓋實際成本,只要出口分攤其所佔全部開支比例。擁有最好國內市場的國家,尤其是產品標準化(如我們的),可以很快賣得比外國生產者更多。我在英國就此使用的說法是:「剩餘定律」。它後來在商業討論中普遍使用。

chapters.title: The Homestead Strike 霍姆斯特德罷工

passages.original: While upon the subject of our manufacturing interests, I may record that on July 1, 1892, during my absence in the Highlands of Scotland, there occurred the one really serious quarrel with our workmen in our whole history. For twenty-six years I had been actively in charge of the relations between ourselves and our men, and it was the pride of my life to think how delightfully satisfactory these had been and were. I hope I fully deserved what my chief partner, Mr. Phipps, said in his letter to the "New York Herald," January 30, 1904, in reply to one who had declared I had remained abroad during the Homestead strike, instead of flying back to support my partners. It was to the effect that "I was always disposed to yield to the demands of the men, however unreasonable"; hence one or two of my partners did not wish me to return. Taking no account of the reward that comes from feeling that you and your employees are friends and judging only from economical results, I believe that higher wages to men who respect their employers and are happy and contented are a good investment, yielding, indeed, big dividends.
passages.vernacular: 講到我哋嘅製造業務,我可以記錄一下:1892年7月1日,我身在蘇格蘭高地期間,發生咗我哋整部歷史中唯一一次真正嚴重嘅工人糾紛。二十六年來,我一直積極負責處理我哋同工人嘅關係,想起呢啲關係曾經同依然多麼令人滿意,係我一生嘅驕傲。我希望我當得起我嘅主要合夥人菲普斯先生在1904年1月30日《紐約先驅報》上嘅信中所講,佢回應一個人,該人聲稱霍姆斯特德罷工期間我留在國外,而不是飛回去支持我嘅合夥人。大意是「我總是傾向於答應工人嘅要求,無論幾無理」;所以我一兩個合夥人不想我返去。撇開你同僱員是朋友所得嘅回報不談,單從經濟結果判斷,我相信向尊重僱主、快樂滿足嘅工人付更高工資係一項好投資,確實帶來大額股息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 講到我們的製造業務,我可以記錄一下:1892年7月1日,我身在蘇格蘭高地期間,發生了我們整部歷史中唯一一次真正嚴重的工人糾紛。二十六年來,我一直積極負責處理我們與工人的關係,想起這些關係曾經和依然多麼令人滿意,是我一生的驕傲。我希望我當得起我的主要合夥人菲普斯先生在1904年1月30日《紐約先驅報》上的信中所說,他回應一個人,該人聲稱霍姆斯特德罷工期間我留在國外,而不是飛回去支持我的合夥人。大意是「我總是傾向於答應工人的要求,無論多無理」;所以我一兩個合夥人不想我回去。撇開你與僱員是朋友所得的回報不談,單從經濟結果判斷,我相信向尊重僱主、快樂滿足的工人付更高工資是一項好投資,確實帶來大額股息。

passages.original: Question: "It was stated that Mr. Carnegie acted in a cowardly manner in not returning to America from Scotland and being present when the strike was in progress at Homestead."
passages.vernacular: 問:「有人話卡內基先生行為懦弱,罷工在霍姆斯特德進行時,冇從蘇格蘭返美國,冇喺場。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 問:「有人說卡內基先生行為懦弱,罷工在霍姆斯特德進行時,沒從蘇格蘭回美國,沒在場。」

passages.original: Answer: "When Mr. Carnegie heard of the trouble at Homestead he immediately wired that he would take the first ship for America, but his partners begged him not to appear, as they were of the opinion that the welfare of the Company required that he should not be in this country at the time. They knew of his extreme disposition to always grant the demands of labor, however unreasonable.
passages.vernacular: 答:「卡內基先生聽到霍姆斯特德嘅麻煩時,即刻發電報話會搭第一班船返美國,不過佢嘅合夥人懇求佢唔好出現,因為佢哋認為公司嘅福祉要求佢當時唔在呢個國家。佢哋知道佢極度傾向於總是答應勞工要求,無論幾無理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 答:「卡內基先生聽到霍姆斯特德的麻煩時,立刻發電報說會搭第一班船回美國,不過他的合夥人懇求他不要出現,因為他們認為公司的福祉要求他當時不在這個國家。他們知道他極度傾向於總是答應勞工要求,無論多無理。

passages.original: "I have never known of any one interested in the business to make any complaint about Mr. Carnegie's absence at that time, but all the partners rejoiced that they were permitted to manage the affair in their own way." (Henry Phipps in the New York Herald, January 30, 1904.)]
passages.vernacular: 「我從未聽聞任何與業務有利益關係嘅人,對卡內基先生當時嘅缺席有任何投訴,所有合夥人都慶幸能夠按自己嘅方式處理此事。」(亨利·菲普斯,《紐約先驅報》,1904年1月30日。)]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從未聽聞任何與業務有利益關係的人,對卡內基先生當時的缺席有任何投訴,所有合夥人都慶幸能夠按自己的方式處理此事。」(亨利·菲普斯,《紐約先驅報》,1904年1月30日。)]

passages.original: The manufacture of steel was revolutionized by the Bessemer open-hearth and basic inventions. The machinery hitherto employed had become obsolete, and our firm, recognizing this, spent several millions at Homestead reconstructing and enlarging the works. The new machinery made about sixty per cent more steel than the old. Two hundred and eighteen tonnage men (that is, men who were paid by the ton of steel produced) were working under a three years' contract, part of the last year being with the new machinery. Thus their earnings had increased almost sixty per cent before the end of the contract.
passages.vernacular: 貝塞麥平爐同鹼性法發明令製鋼革命化。迄今使用嘅機器已經過時,我哋公司認識到這點,在霍姆斯特德花咗數百萬重建同擴大工廠。新機器造出嘅鋼比舊機器多大約百分之六十。二百一十八名計噸工人(即按所產鋼噸數付酬嘅工人)按三年合約工作,最後一年部分時間使用新機器。所以合約結束前,佢哋嘅收入已增加近百分之六十。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝塞麥平爐和鹼性法發明使製鋼革命化。迄今使用的機器已經過時,我們公司認識到這點,在霍姆斯特德花了數百萬重建和擴大工廠。新機器造出的鋼比舊機器多大約百分之六十。二百一十八名計噸工人(即按所產鋼噸數付酬的工人)按三年合約工作,最後一年部分時間使用新機器。所以合約結束前,他們的收入已增加近百分之六十。

passages.original: The firm offered to divide this sixty per cent with them in the new scale to be made thereafter. That is to say, the earnings of the men would have been thirty per cent greater than under the old scale and the other thirty per cent would have gone to the firm to recompense it for its outlay. The work of the men would not have been much harder than it had been hitherto, as the improved machinery did the work. This was not only fair and liberal, it was generous, and under ordinary circumstances would have been accepted by the men with thanks. But the firm was then engaged in making armor for the United States Government, which we had declined twice to manufacture and which was urgently needed. It had also the contract to furnish material for the Chicago Exhibition. Some of the leaders of the men, knowing these conditions, insisted upon demanding the whole sixty per cent, thinking the firm would be compelled to give it. The firm could not agree, nor should it have agreed to such an attempt as this to take it by the throat and say, "Stand and deliver." It very rightly declined. Had I been at home nothing would have induced me to yield to this unfair attempt to extort.
passages.vernacular: 公司提出,在之後訂立嘅新工資表中,與佢哋平分這百分之六十。即係話,工人收入會比舊工資表高百分之三十,另外百分之三十歸公司,補償其支出。工人嘅工作不會比以前辛苦多少,因為改良嘅機器做了工作。呢不單公平慷慨,而且係大方,喺普通情況下工人會感謝接受。不過公司當時正為美國政府製造裝甲,我哋曾兩次拒絕製造,而且急需。公司亦有合約為芝加哥博覽會提供材料。工人一些領袖知道呢啲情況,堅持要求全部百分之六十,以為公司會被迫答應。公司唔能夠同意,亦唔應該該同意呢種掐住佢咽喉、講「站住,交出嚟」嘅企圖。公司十分正確地拒絕。如果我在家,世上冇任何事會令我屈服於呢種不公平嘅勒索企圖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公司提出,在之後訂立的新工資表中,與他們平分這百分之六十。即是說,工人收入會比舊工資表高百分之三十,另外百分之三十歸公司,補償其支出。工人的工作不會比以前辛苦多少,因為改良的機器做了工作。這不僅公平慷慨,而且是大方,在普通情況下工人會感謝接受。不過公司當時正為美國政府製造裝甲,我們曾兩次拒絕製造,而且急需。公司也有合約為芝加哥博覽會提供材料。工人一些領袖知道這些情況,堅持要求全部百分之六十,以為公司會被迫答應。公司不能同意,也不應該同意這種掐住它咽喉、說「站住,交出來」的企圖。公司十分正確地拒絕。如果我在家,世上沒任何事會使我屈服於這種不公平的勒索企圖。

passages.original: Up to this point all had been right enough. The policy I had pursued in cases of difference with our men was that of patiently waiting, reasoning with them, and showing them that their demands were unfair; but never attempting to employ new men in their places--never. The superintendent of Homestead, however, was assured by the three thousand men who were not concerned in the dispute that they could run the works, and were anxious to rid themselves of the two hundred and eighteen men who had banded themselves into a union and into which they had hitherto refused to admit those in other departments--only the "heaters" and "rollers" of steel being eligible.
passages.vernacular: 到此為止一切都相當正確。我在與工人意見不合時一貫奉行的方針,是耐心等待,同佢哋講道理,向佢哋顯示佢哋嘅要求不公平;但從不嘗試僱用新人取代佢哋——從不。不過霍姆斯特德總管獲三千名與爭議無關嘅工人保證,佢哋可以運作工廠,並急於擺脫結成工會嘅二百一十八人——工會迄今拒絕接納其他部門嘅人——只有鋼嘅「加熱工」同「軋鋼工」才有資格。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到此為止一切都相當正確。我在與工人意見不合時一貫奉行的方針,是耐心等待,跟他們講道理,向他們顯示他們的要求不公平;但從不嘗試僱用新人取代他們——從不。不過霍姆斯特德總管獲三千名與爭議無關的工人保證,他們可以運作工廠,並急於擺脫結成工會的二百一十八人——工會迄今拒絕接納其他部門的人——只有鋼的「加熱工」和「軋鋼工」才有資格。

passages.original: My partners were misled by this superintendent, who was himself misled. He had not had great experience in such affairs, having recently been promoted from a subordinate position. The unjust demands of the few union men, and the opinion of the three thousand non-union men that they were unjust, very naturally led him into thinking there would be no trouble and that the workmen would do as they had promised. There were many men among the three thousand who could take, and wished to take, the places of the two hundred and eighteen--at least so it was reported to me.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅合夥人被呢位總管誤導,而總管自己也被誤導。佢對此類事務缺乏豐富經驗,最近才從下級職位晉升。少數工會成員不公平嘅要求,同三千名非工會工人認為其不公平嘅意見,很自然令佢以為不會有麻煩,工人會按承諾行事。三千人當中有許多人可以、而且願意取代二百一十八人——至少有人咁樣向我報告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的合夥人被這位總管誤導,而總管自己也被誤導。他對此類事務缺乏豐富經驗,最近才從下級職位晉升。少數工會成員不公平的要求,和三千名非工會工人認為其不公平的意見,很自然使他以為不會有麻煩,工人會按承諾行事。三千人當中有許多人可以、而且願意取代二百一十八人——至少有人這樣向我報告。

passages.original: It is easy to look back and say that the vital step of opening the works should never have been taken. All the firm had to do was to say to the men: "There is a labor dispute here and you must settle it between yourselves. The firm has made you a most liberal offer. The works will run when the dispute is adjusted, and not till then. Meanwhile your places remain open to you." Or, it might have been well if the superintendent had said to the three thousand men, "All right, if you will come and run the works without protection," thus throwing upon them the responsibility of protecting themselves--three thousand men as against two hundred and eighteen. Instead of this it was thought advisable (as an additional precaution by the state officials, I understand) to have the sheriff with guards to protect the thousands against the hundreds. The leaders of the latter were violent and aggressive men; they had guns and pistols, and, as was soon proved, were able to intimidate the thousands.
passages.vernacular: 事後回顧,容易講開工呢關鍵一步本唔應該該採取。公司只需要對工人講:「這裡有勞資糾紛,你哋必須自己解決。公司已向你哋提出最慷慨的建議。糾紛解決時工廠就會開工,喺此之前唔會。同時你哋嘅位置為你哋保留。」或者,如果總管對三千名工人講:「好,如果你哋願意在冇保護下來運作工廠」,從而把保護自己嘅責任推畀佢哋——三千人對二百一十八人——也許更好。相反,我了解到,有人認為(作為州官員額外預防措施)明智嘅做法係安排郡長帶衛兵保護數千人對抗數百人。後者嘅領袖是暴力好鬥嘅人;佢哋有槍同手槍,而且很快證明能夠恐嚇數千人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事後回顧,容易說開工這關鍵一步本不應該採取。公司只需要對工人說:「這裡有勞資糾紛,你們必須自己解決。公司已向你們提出最慷慨的建議。糾紛解決時工廠就會開工,在此之前不會。同時你們的位置為你們保留。」或者,如果總管對三千名工人說:「好,如果你們願意在沒保護下來運作工廠」,從而把保護自己的責任推給他們——三千人對二百一十八人——也許更好。相反,我了解到,有人認為(作為州官員額外預防措施)明智的做法是安排郡長帶衛兵保護數千人對抗數百人。後者的領袖是暴力好鬥的人;他們有槍和手槍,而且很快證明能夠恐嚇數千人。

passages.original: I quote what I once laid down in writing as our rule: "My idea is that the Company should be known as determined to let the men at any works stop work; that it will confer freely with them and wait patiently until they decide to return to work, never thinking of trying new men--never." The best men as men, and the best workmen, are not walking the streets looking for work. Only the inferior class as a rule is idle. The kind of men we desired are rarely allowed to lose their jobs, even in dull times. It is impossible to get new men to run successfully the complicated machinery of a modern steel plant. The attempt to put in new men converted the thousands of old men who desired to work, into lukewarm supporters of our policy, for workmen can always be relied upon to resent the employment of new men. Who can blame them?
passages.vernacular: 我引述我曾寫下作為我哋規則嘅話:「我嘅想法是,公司應被知道決心讓任何工廠嘅工人停工;會自由同佢哋商議,耐心等待直到佢哋決定返工,從不想嘗試新人——從不。」最好嘅人作為人,最好嘅工人,不會在街上走來走去找工作。一般只有次一等嘅人才閒置。我哋想要嘅那種人,即使在淡季也很少被允許失去工作。不可能找到新人成功運作現代鋼廠複雜嘅機器。嘗試引入新人,將數千名想工作嘅老工人轉變成對我哋方針嘅冷淡支持者,因為工人總是可以預期會憎恨僱用新人。邊個能責怪佢哋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我引述我曾寫下作為我們規則的話:「我的想法是,公司應被知道決心讓任何工廠的工人停工;會自由與他們商議,耐心等待直到他們決定回工,從不想嘗試新人——從不。」最好的人作為人,最好的工人,不會在街上走來走去找工作。一般只有次一等的人才閒置。我們想要的那種人,即使在淡季也很少被允許失去工作。不可能找到新人成功運作現代鋼廠複雜的機器。嘗試引入新人,將數千名想工作的老工人轉變成對我們方針的冷淡支持者,因為工人總是可以預期會憎恨僱用新人。誰能責怪他們?

passages.original: If I had been at home, however, I might have been persuaded to open the works, as the superintendent desired, to test whether our old men would go to work as they had promised. But it should be noted that the works were not opened at first by my partners for new men. On the contrary, it was, as I was informed upon my return, at the wish of the thousands of our old men that they were opened. This is a vital point. My partners were in no way blamable for making the trial so recommended by the superintendent. Our rule never to employ new men, but to wait for the old to return, had not been violated so far. In regard to the second opening of the works, after the strikers had shot the sheriff's officers, it is also easy to look back and say, "How much better had the works been closed until the old men voted to return"; but the Governor of Pennsylvania, with eight thousand troops, had meanwhile taken charge of the situation.
passages.vernacular: 不過如果我在家,我可能被說服按總管所願開工,以測試我哋嘅老工人是否按承諾上工。但應注意,我嘅合夥人起初開工並不是為了新人。相反,我返嚟後獲知,是應我哋數千名老工人嘅意願而開工。這是關鍵一點。我嘅合夥人作出總管推薦嘅嘗試,絕不應受責備。我哋從不僱用新人、等待老工人返來嘅規則,到目前為止未被違反。關於罷工者槍擊郡長手下後第二次開工,事後都容易講「如果工廠關閉到老工人投票返工,多好」;但賓夕法尼亞州長已帶八千軍隊接管局面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過如果我在家,我可能被說服按總管所願開工,以測試我們的老工人是否按承諾上工。但應注意,我的合夥人起初開工並不是為了新人。相反,我回來後獲知,是應我們數千名老工人的意願而開工。這是關鍵一點。我的合夥人作出總管推薦的嘗試,絕不應受責備。我們從不僱用新人、等待老工人回來的規則,到目前為止未被違反。關於罷工者槍擊郡長手下後第二次開工,事後也容易說「如果工廠關閉到老工人投票回工,多好」;但賓夕法尼亞州長已帶八千軍隊接管局面。

passages.original: I was traveling in the Highlands of Scotland when the trouble arose, and did not hear of it until two days after. Nothing I have ever had to meet in all my life, before or since, wounded me so deeply. No pangs remain of any wound received in my business career save that of Homestead. It was so unnecessary. The men were outrageously wrong. The strikers, with the new machinery, would have made from four to nine dollars a day under the new scale--thirty per cent more than they were making with the old machinery. While in Scotland I received the following cable from the officers of the union of our workmen:
passages.vernacular: 麻煩發生時,我正在蘇格蘭高地旅行,兩日後才聽聞。我一生中無論之前或之後遇到的任何事,都冇像它那樣深深傷害我。我事業中所受嘅任何創傷,只有霍姆斯特德仍留下痛楚。佢係如此唔使要。工人極其錯誤。罷工者用新機器,喺新工資表下每日可以賺四至九元——比用舊機器賺嘅多百分之三十。我在蘇格蘭時,收到我哋工人工會職員嘅以下電報:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 麻煩發生時,我正在蘇格蘭高地旅行,兩天後才聽聞。我一生中無論之前或之後遇到的任何事,都沒像它那樣深深傷害我。我事業中所受的任何創傷,只有霍姆斯特德仍留下痛楚。它是如此不必要。工人極其錯誤。罷工者用新機器,在新工資表下每天可以賺四至九元——比用舊機器賺的多百分之三十。我在蘇格蘭時,收到我們工人工會職員的以下電報:

passages.original: "Kind master, tell us what you wish us to do and we shall do it for you."
passages.vernacular: 「好心嘅主人,告訴我哋你想我哋做咩,我哋會為你做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好心的主人,告訴我們你想我們做什麼,我們會為你做。」

passages.original: This was most touching, but, alas, too late. The mischief was done, the works were in the hands of the Governor; it was too late.
passages.vernacular: 呢極為動人,但唉,太遲喇。禍已闖,工廠喺州長手中;太遲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這極為動人,但唉,太遲了。禍已闖,工廠在州長手中;太遲了。

passages.original: I received, while abroad, numerous kind messages from friends conversant with the circumstances, who imagined my unhappiness. The following from Mr. Gladstone was greatly appreciated:
passages.vernacular: 我在國外時,收到許多熟悉情況嘅朋友嘅善意訊息,佢哋想像我嘅不快樂。格萊斯頓先生以下一封,我極為感激:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在國外時,收到許多熟悉情況的朋友的善意訊息,他們想像我的不快樂。格萊斯頓先生以下一封,我極為感激:

passages.original: My wife has long ago offered her thanks, with my own, for your most kind congratulations. But I do not forget that you have been suffering yourself from anxieties, and have been exposed to imputations in connection with your gallant efforts to direct rich men into a course of action more enlightened than that which they usually follow. I wish I could relieve you from these imputations of journalists, too often rash, conceited or censorious, rancorous, ill-natured.
